items.title: Path of Valheiman DB
items.text:
A datamined reference for Path of Valheiman, the Path of Exile–inspired passive tree, crafting and loot overhaul for Valheim.

Every page here is generated from the mod's own files. The text is produced by the game's own code, so it matches what you see in game and updates with each patch.

Planning a build?

To plan your own build or explore builds shared by other players, head to povbuilds.com, the Path of Valheiman build planner.

items.title: Passive tree
items.text:
• Passive Tree Viewer: the full tree, searchable
  • Keystones: build-defining passives with a drawback
  • Notables: the larger passives, by category
  • Masteries: passives where you choose one option

items.title: Crafting
items.text:
• Craft Tree Viewer: the craft tree, with sectors and professions
  • Professions: each profession and its notables
  • Craft Notables and Craft Masteries
  • Buildings: the mod's kiln, rune carver table, gate, vacuum chest and wild sowing

items.title: Items
items.text:
• Mods: every property an item can roll, with tiers and weights
  • Item bases: weapons, armour, shields and trinkets, with stats and recipes
  • Currency: runes, essences, sigils and crafting materials
  • Jewels: base and unique jewels, and the properties base jewels roll
  • Uniques: unique jewels and belts, with their lines and where they drop

items.title: Monsters
items.text:
• Monster Modifiers: what starred creatures can roll, with their values
  • Bosses: the mod's bosses, how to summon them and what every boss drops
  • Creatures: runic kin and the creatures of the Blight Mist

items.title: Mechanics
items.text:
• Creature scaling: level, health and damage, stars, difficulty, Monster Power
  • Experience and levels: area and item levels, recommended player levels, experience fall-off
  • Loot and experience: what a kill drops and the experience it gives
  • Combat and building: critical strikes, evasion, resistances, enemy penetration, build cost

items.title: Patches
items.text: • Patches: what each update changed in the game data, compared with the version before

items.title: Keywords
items.text:
Underlined keywords link to their entry from the mod's in-game wiki, and show its definition on hover. Use the search bar to look up any passive or keyword.

Unimplemented content

The game files contain content that isn't finished yet, like placeholder passives or stats without proper text. It is listed here too, marked Unimplemented or Unfinished text.

items.title: Credits
items.text:
Path of Valheiman is made by treextr: mod page · Discord · Patreon · Boosty.

This is an unofficial fan site. All game data, names, text and node art belong to the mod author. This site does not host or redistribute the mod. Get it from the official page.

items.title: How it works
items.text: The mod ships its passive tree, craft tree, loot tables and translations as data embedded in its DLL. This site reads that data and generates every page from it. There is no manual data entry.

items.title: Buildings
items.text:
The pieces Path of Valheiman adds to the Hammer and the Cultivator. Each is built on a Valheim piece, with the mod's own look, cost and use.

Name Effect Azurite Kiln Grinds azurite into dust Rune Carver Table The crafting station for the mod's own items: runes, punches, sigils, rings, belts... Inscription Gate A Runecarver's portal: inscribe which portal of the world it leads to. Shift + use: inscribe the link. Vacuum Chest Pulls finished goods from nearby smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills, and feeds them from its contents. Shift + wheel: radius. Shift + use: what to collect. Wild Sowing Wild growth. Planted on cultivated ground.

Passives that change building in general (cheaper pieces, less rain wear, station range...) are on the craft tree.

Data from Path of Valheiman 5.3.2, extracted 2026-10-24.

items.title: Craft Masteries
items.text: Options you choose on mastery passives. Each option is listed once, with the number of tree nodes that offer it; open an option for its full description and where to find it.

items.title: Beekeeper
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Cosy Hives 3% increased hive filling speed per point of comfortHives fill faster the more comfort there is around them 12 Guard Bees Bees sting enemies near your hives 12 Hive Chain Harvesting a hive collects from neighbouring hives one after another, hive by hive along the chain, not by area 12 Honey Stores Hives you built hold 2 times as much honey 12 Swarm Split Once a day an own hive that is full, its honey not yet taken, has a 5% chance to yield a queen beeOnce a day a hive you built that is full, with its honey not yet taken, has a 5% chance to yield a queen bee 12 Wildflower Meadow Own hives fill 5% faster for every flowering plant nearby (dandelion, thistle, flax, barley), up to 50%Hives you built fill faster for every flowering plant growing nearby (dandelion, thistle, flax, barley) 12 Winter Hive Hives you built work in cold biomes 12

items.title: Builder
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Auto Doors Doors you build open as anyone approaches and close behind them 10 Careful Builder You cannot damage player-built pieces 10 Floor as Roof Floors you build are a full roof: what is under them stays dry, is sheltered from rain and counts as under a roof for fires, beds, rest and stations 10 Hugin's Flight {key.hugin}, with a building tool in hand, sends the sight aloft as Hugin: the body hovers in place and pieces are placed within building range of the raven, up to 30 m from the body; [Space] rises, [Ctrl] sinks, [Shift] flies faster, {key.hugin} again returnsWith a hammer or hoe in hand, press B to send your sight aloft like Odin's raven and build from the air while your body stays safe on the ground. The view flies up to 30 m from you; pieces are placed within your Building range of the view and still need a workbench in reach and your materials 10 Light Frame Pieces you built lose only 50% of the usual support 10 Nearby Chests (building) Building draws materials from nearby chests 10 No Bounds Build and remove pieces where building is forbidden: dungeons, boss altars, traders' camps and other no-build places 10 Open-Air Bench The bench works under open sky 10 Weatherproof Pieces you built take no damage from rain, water or waves 10

items.title: Cook
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Batch Cook Placing raw food on a cooking station fills every free spot at once from your inventory 11 Double Pot The cauldron cooks two recipes at once 11 Fresh Kitchen Your own cooking does not degrade: full bonuses until the end of its duration 11 Hearth Comfort 3% increased cooking speed per point of comfortCooking stations near you cook faster with every point of comfort, the way hives do 11 Kitchen Bell Food on your cooking stations rings when it is done and is marked on the minimap until you take it 11 Watchful cook Food on the hearth no longer burns 11

items.title: Farmer
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Any Soil Planted growth grows in any biome. Cultivated ground and growing space are still required 12 Bed Watch Aiming at a plant in your beds shows how long it has left until it ripens 12 Broad Sowing Mass planting: hold {0} and a whole bed goes in at once. With {0} the wheel rotates the bed, with {0} and Alt it changes the spacing between plants 12 Irrigation ×2 crop and sapling growth speedOwn crops grow faster 12 Quick Replant Picking a crop plants it again on the spot, if you carry its seed 12 Scarecrow Crops near your buildings are not trampled or eaten 12 Tight Beds Plants need 50% of the usual spacing when planted 12

items.title: Fisher
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Deep Cast Fishing cast range is 2 times longer 12 Line Keeper The fishing line never snaps 12 Native Bait Fishing needs no bait and never spends it, even when you carry bait: every fish at the float bites as if on its own bait, ocean included. No boss kill is required. 12 Quick Haul A hooked fish closer than 5 m comes out at once, without the fightA fish pulled closer than 5 m comes out at once, without the fight 12 Sea Legs Fishing from a ship never tips the rod 12 Shoal Sight Fish shoals in your view radius are marked on the map 12

items.title: Forager
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Cuttings Picking a wild plant has a 6% chance to give its seed; wild plants are sown only from their seedsForaging a wild plant has a 6% chance to give its seed. Wild plants have seeds of their own now, and this mastery is the only way to get them 9 Double Pick Anything picked by hand (berries, mushrooms, branches, stones, tar, honey) has a 15% chance to give twiceAnything you pick up by interacting (berries, mushrooms, branches, stones, tar, honey) has a 15% chance to give twice 9 Forager's Nose You smell berries, mushrooms and flowers: faint streaks drift toward you from the nearest ones 9 Night Forager At night, pickables near you glow and give 1 extra 9 On the Move Picking bushes, branches, stones and other resources does not stop a run: the hands reach for the find while the legs keep running. 9 Snacking Raw berries and mushrooms are eaten as a snack: half their effect, without taking a food slot; up to 3 different snacks at onceRaw berries and mushrooms you eat give their effect at 50% strength without taking a food slot, up to 3 at once 9 Weightless Forage Foraging materials weigh nothing while they are in your inventory 9 Windfall While you are in the air, everything below you is shaken loose: berries, mushrooms and branches fall to the ground and hives give up their honey , you still have to pick it all up yourself Tar pits count too. 9

items.title: Herder

Each animal keeps its own stats: a wolf is quick but pulls little, a lox is slow and pulls a lot. Design to be worked out 8 Herd Call Commanding one tamed animal commands every tamed animal within 30 m; a follower left farther than that stays behindTamed animals within 30 m follow you as a group; step farther away and they stay behind, so you can break off 8 Stable Keeper Tamed animals near a building you built stay fed 2 times as long 8

One bait at a time; it lasts 60 s or until eaten 10 Clean kill A beast killed in one hit always drops its trophy 10 Field Dressing Hides and meat from your kills go straight into your inventory 10 Nearby Chests (supplies) Crafting supplies - ammo, bombs, food, mead, oils and materials - can use materials from accessible nearby chests. 37 Pack Hunter Tamed wolves near you bring the hides of their kills to you 10 Rare Sight Rare and unique creatures within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap; the marks clear as soon as they leave that radius 10 Tracker's Eye You see animal tracks 10

items.text: Option Effect Nodes Cascade A shattered deposit has a 5% chance to shatter a random deposit nearby; each such shatter rolls againShattering a deposit has a 5% chance to Shatter a random deposit nearby. The chance cascades: each deposit it Shatters rolls again, so with enough luck a whole mine bursts in a chain 17 Clean Split A seam your pickaxe beats by two tiers shatters in one blow 17 Focused Seam Weak spots of the mining mini-game appear only on the deposit being mined 17 Hidden Vein 5% chance that a hit on stone knocks out a random ore of a biome whose boss has been defeated on the server5% chance that Mining stone knocks out a random ore from a biome whose boss you have defeated 17 Ore Portals Ore and metal bars pass through portals once the boss of their biome is dead; the portal keeps a share of what passes (25%).• Copper, tin, bronze — The Elder• Iron — Bonemass• Silver — Moder• Black metal — Yagluth• Flametal — Fader 17 Ore Sight Ore deposits within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap; the marks clear as soon as they leave that radius 17 Precise Strike Every hit into a weak spot also yields an extra share of the deposit’s ore. 17 Runecarver mastery Reserved: this profession is not designed yet.Unimplemented 1 Smelted Lode 5% chance that ore drops already smelted, as its bar 17

items.title: Pathfinder
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Field Portal You can build and dismantle portals without a workbench 13 Grave Tether When you die, your equipped gear, hotbar and food slots stay on you, and your grave is marked on the map until it is emptied 13 Momentum Slide Crouch while running fast or right after landing a jump to slide along the ground, keeping your speed. 13 Night Walker Every at Night bonus, combat and crafting alike, also works in the evening 13 Pull-Up Hold jump and push toward a wall while in the air to pull yourself up onto a ledge within reach. A pull-up costs 15 stamina, a low ledge half as much. A short tap of jump near a wall stays a wall rebound. 13 Quick Mark Shift + Y marks what you are looking at on your map with its own icon and name 13 Shared Map Standing near another player, you exchange explored map and pins with them 13 Sleep by the Fire You can sleep sitting at a fire: no bed and no roof needed, and the night passes even if someone on the server has not lain down 13 Sliding Down a Slope Crouched on a slope, the character rides down faster than running. 13 Trail Runner Running on a trail or a paved road costs 25% less staminaRunning on a trail costs 25% less stamina 13

items.title: Relic seeker
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Belt Lantern The Dvergr lantern hangs on your belt in its own equipment slot 11 Breadcrumbs Inside a dungeon the minimap draws the corridors you have walked, in the game's own map style 11 Chest Sight Chests in your view radius are marked on the map 11 Dungeon Sight Dungeon entrances within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap; the marks clear as soon as they leave that radius 11 Every Door Any door, built or in a dungeon, opens as you come up to it and closes behind you. A door with a key still needs the key in your bag. 11 Magic Purse A purse appears to the right of the inventory and collects your coins. Coins in the purse weigh nothing and are kept on death. 11 Return Path Once per dungeon, sitting down offers a flight to its exit for 3 surtling coresOnce per dungeon, sit down to fly to its exit for 3 surtling cores. If the dungeon is reset, the flight is available again. 11 Second Sweep Chests anywhere in the world that the character has emptied fully refill after a few in-game days, again and again, with fresh loot of their biome (Chest item quantity, Chest item rarity and Extra item apply). Aiming at such a chest shows the time left until it refills 11 Tidy Pack Two buttons in the bag: stack into nearby chests and sort the bag 11 Treasure Map Opening a chest has a 30% chance to mark the nearest unopened chest on the map; the mark goes once the chest is emptied 11

items.title: Runecarver
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Ascendant Rune +10% chance that a property added by a rune rises one tierWhen a rune adds or raises a property, it has a chance to rise one tier more as a separate step, beyond the item's level limit. You see a second flash, hear a chime and read "+1 affix tier". 10 Azurite Sight Azurite veins within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap: plain, corrupted and divine each with its own icon. A vein mined out by more than three quarters is no longer marked. 10 Chisel Quarrying Rune chisels also mine stone and ore deposits, like a pickaxe of the same metal: bronze, iron or black metal (flametal hits as hard as black metal). A deposit too hard for that pickaxe is too hard for the chisel. Chisel hits do not train the Pickaxes skill. Azurite veins are mined as before. 10 Divine Touch +2% chance for divine azuriteEach chisel hit on a plain azurite vein outside the mist has a chance to turn it divine, with the same lightning as a heavenly strike. Any chisel works, in any biome. 10 Inscription Gate You can build the Inscription Gate, a Runecarver portal with pink-violet runes. Shift + use on it opens the map of every portal in the world: pick one and inscribe the link, and everyone who enters the gate steps out there. 10 Perfect Inscription +10% chance that a property rolled by a rune takes the highest value of its tierA property rolled by a rune (Fate included) has a chance to take the highest value of its tier. 10 Portal Crate Away from a workbench, dismantling a portal packs it into a crate that keeps its tag, author, durability and Inscription Gate link. Place it back from the crate anywhere. A crate cannot pass through a portal. 10 Relic Passage Dragon eggs for summoning, Hildir's chests and dvergr parts (charred cogwheels, dvergr needles, mechanical springs) go through portals, with no portal toll. Ore and metal are not included. 10 Vacuum Chest Unlocks the Vacuum Chest at the Rune Carver Table. It takes finished goods from smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills around it and feeds them from its contents. Shift + mouse wheel sets the radius, Shift + E the kind of goods it collects. 10

items.title: Shipwright
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Anchor Ships the character builds carry an anchor: anyone aiming at the helm drops or raises it with Shift+E. An anchored ship holds its place, still rocking on the waves and turning with the wind. 19 Deep Hold Ships you built carry one more row of cargo 19 Harbor Mark Your ships are marked on the map with a ship icon wherever they are 19 Mending at Sea Ships can be repaired with the hammer without a workbench nearby 19 Open Shipyard Ships can be built and taken apart with the hammer anywhere, without a workbench. Away from a workbench a ship is not broken into materials: it is packed into a crate together with its cargo, and the crate on the hotbar sets the same ship back on the water - with its hull, its builder, every shipwright property and everything that was in its hold. Nobody may stand aboard a ship being taken apart. 19 Salvage Float Nothing is lost to the sea: a ship's hold and items sunk in deep water float up in crates that stay put and are marked on the map until emptied 19 Storm Keel Ships you built keep full control in storms 19 Weather Sense The coming weather and when it arrives are shown under the minimap 19

items.title: Smith
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Balanced Blade 10% increased damage with Smith equipmentCrafting or upgrading weapons using Smith materials has a 25% chance to add an item affix that increases their damage. Each eligible mastery rolls independently. 10 Chest Feed Smelters and kilns pull ore and coal from nearby chests on their own, with the bonuses of the chest owner. Placing a smelter shows the pull radius with the same ring as crafting from nearby chests. Works with every smelter, kiln and chest in the game 10 Fitted Plate 10% increased armour with Smith equipmentCrafting or upgrading heavy armour has a 25% chance to add an item affix that increases its armour. Each eligible mastery rolls independently. 10 Forge Comfort 3% increased smelting and charcoal kiln speed per point of comfortSmelters, kilns and forges near you work faster with every point of comfort, the way hives do 10 Master's Mark Allows upgrading Smith equipment one quality level beyond its normal maximum. Items without upgrades remain unupgradeable. Both profession masteries on a mixed recipe extend its limit only once. Station and material requirements still apply. 10 Whetstones Whetstones can be crafted at the forge. Right-click a whetstone, then left-click equipment to restore 25% durability, up to its metal tier.You can craft whetstones: a consumable that repairs the weapon or tool in your hands by 25%, away from any workbench. Each metal tier has its own whetstone 10

items.title: Tanner
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Auto Repair Interacting with any crafting station repairs on its own every item that station can repair 11 Balanced Grip Self-crafted weapons cost 10% less stamina to attack with Tanner equipmentCrafting or upgrading weapons using Tanner materials has a 25% chance to add an item affix that reduces their attack stamina cost. Each eligible mastery rolls independently. 11 Fitted Set Allows upgrading Tanner equipment one quality level beyond its normal maximum. Items without upgrades remain unupgradeable. Both profession masteries on a mixed recipe extend its limit only once. Station and material requirements still apply. 11 Loom Chain Spinning wheels pull flax from nearby chests, with the bonuses of the chest owner 11 Nearby Chests (equipment) Crafting and upgrading equipment - weapons, armour, shields and tools - can use materials from accessible nearby chests. 21 Padded Fit Self-crafted armor weighs 25% less with Tanner equipmentCrafting or upgrading light armour has a 25% chance to add an item affix that reduces its weight. Each eligible mastery rolls independently. 11

items.title: Woodcutter
items.text:
Option Effect Nodes Ancient Grain Extra wood rolls 2 times on ancient, fine and Yggdrasil wood 16 Clean Felling Trees you fell leave no stump: the wood the stump would give drops together with the trunk 16 Clean Trunk A tree your axe beats by two tiers falls in one blow 16 Guided Fall A tree you fell always falls the way you were looking at your last hit 16 Seed Scatter An Extra seed from Chopping can turn out to be a random tree seed from a biome whose boss you have defeated, not only the seed of the tree you are chopping 16 Steady Series Every hit of a chopping series knocks out an Extra log 16 Stump Breaker An axe's alternate attack splits any stump in one blow 16 Timber Luck A falling tree cannot kill you: the damage lands, but you are left at 1 health. 16

Data from Path of Valheiman 5.3.2, extracted 2026-10-24.

items.title: Open Shipyard
items.text: Craft mastery option · Shipwright

items.title: Description
items.text:
What the game shows when you hover the option, alongside the effect above.

Ships can be built and taken apart with the hammer anywhere, without a workbench. Away from a workbench a ship is not broken into materials: it is packed into a crate together with its cargo, and the crate on the hotbar sets the same ship back on the water - with its hull, its builder, every shipwright property and everything that was in its hold. Nobody may stand aboard a ship being taken apart.

items.title: Keyword: Open Shipyard
items.text: Allows building and dismantling ships without a workbench. Away from a workbench, dismantling packs the ship and cargo into a crate; deploying it restores the same ship. Nobody may be aboard during packing. Dismantle with the hammer ([Mouse 3]); to deploy, select the crate on the hotbar and place the ship like any build piece. The crate goes through portals while its hold carries nothing a portal refuses.

items.title: Helmsman
items.text:
Craft notable · Table · Shipwright · Show on tree

10% increased ship speed

items.title: Mastery options
items.text: Option Effect Anchor Ships the character builds carry an anchor: anyone aiming at the helm drops or raises it with Shift+E. An anchored ship holds its place, still rocking on the waves and turning with the wind. Open Shipyard Ships can be built and taken apart with the hammer anywhere, without a workbench. Away from a workbench a ship is not broken into materials: it is packed into a crate together with its cargo, and the crate on the hotbar sets the same ship back on the water - with its hull, its builder, every shipwright property and everything that was in its hold. Nobody may stand aboard a ship being taken apart. Mending at Sea Ships can be repaired with the hammer without a workbench nearby Salvage Float Nothing is lost to the sea: a ship's hold and items sunk in deep water float up in crates that stay put and are marked on the map until emptied Storm Keel Ships you built keep full control in storms Harbor Mark Your ships are marked on the map with a ship icon wherever they are Deep Hold Ships you built carry one more row of cargo Weather Sense The coming weather and when it arrives are shown under the minimap

items.title: Mastery options
items.text: Option Effect Anchor Ships the character builds carry an anchor: anyone aiming at the helm drops or raises it with Shift+E. An anchored ship holds its place, still rocking on the waves and turning with the wind. Open Shipyard Ships can be built and taken apart with the hammer anywhere, without a workbench. Away from a workbench a ship is not broken into materials: it is packed into a crate together with its cargo, and the crate on the hotbar sets the same ship back on the water - with its hull, its builder, every shipwright property and everything that was in its hold. Nobody may stand aboard a ship being taken apart. Mending at Sea Ships can be repaired with the hammer without a workbench nearby Salvage Float Nothing is lost to the sea: a ship's hold and items sunk in deep water float up in crates that stay put and are marked on the map until emptied Storm Keel Ships you built keep full control in storms Harbor Mark Your ships are marked on the map with a ship icon wherever they are Deep Hold Ships you built carry one more row of cargo Weather Sense The coming weather and when it arrives are shown under the minimap

items.title: Carry weight
items.text:
Craft notable · Beast · Runecarver · Show on tree

+30 carry weight

items.title: Mastery options
items.text: Option Effect Inscription Gate You can build the Inscription Gate, a Runecarver portal with pink-violet runes. Shift + use on it opens the map of every portal in the world: pick one and inscribe the link, and everyone who enters the gate steps out there. Azurite Sight Azurite veins within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap: plain, corrupted and divine each with its own icon. A vein mined out by more than three quarters is no longer marked. Divine Touch +2% chance for divine azuriteEach chisel hit on a plain azurite vein outside the mist has a chance to turn it divine, with the same lightning as a heavenly strike. Any chisel works, in any biome. Ascendant Rune +10% chance that a property added by a rune rises one tierWhen a rune adds or raises a property, it has a chance to rise one tier more as a separate step, beyond the item's level limit. You see a second flash, hear a chime and read "+1 affix tier". Perfect Inscription +10% chance that a property rolled by a rune takes the highest value of its tierA property rolled by a rune (Fate included) has a chance to take the highest value of its tier. Portal Crate Away from a workbench, dismantling a portal packs it into a crate that keeps its tag, author, durability and Inscription Gate link. Place it back from the crate anywhere. A crate cannot pass through a portal. Relic Passage Dragon eggs for summoning, Hildir's chests and dvergr parts (charred cogwheels, dvergr needles, mechanical springs) go through portals, with no portal toll. Ore and metal are not included. Vacuum Chest Unlocks the Vacuum Chest at the Rune Carver Table. It takes finished goods from smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills around it and feeds them from its contents. Shift + mouse wheel sets the radius, Shift + E the kind of goods it collects. Chisel Quarrying Rune chisels also mine stone and ore deposits, like a pickaxe of the same metal: bronze, iron or black metal (flametal hits as hard as black metal). A deposit too hard for that pickaxe is too hard for the chisel. Chisel hits do not train the Pickaxes skill. Azurite veins are mined as before.

items.title: Mastery options
items.text: Option Effect Nearby Chests (equipment) Crafting and upgrading equipment - weapons, armour, shields and tools - can use materials from accessible nearby chests. Master's Mark Allows upgrading Smith equipment one quality level beyond its normal maximum. Items without upgrades remain unupgradeable. Both profession masteries on a mixed recipe extend its limit only once. Station and material requirements still apply. Chest Feed Smelters and kilns pull ore and coal from nearby chests on their own, with the bonuses of the chest owner. Placing a smelter shows the pull radius with the same ring as crafting from nearby chests. Works with every smelter, kiln and chest in the game Balanced Blade 10% increased damage with Smith equipmentCrafting or upgrading weapons using Smith materials has a 25% chance to add an item affix that increases their damage. Each eligible mastery rolls independently. Whetstones Whetstones can be crafted at the forge. Right-click a whetstone, then left-click equipment to restore 25% durability, up to its metal tier.You can craft whetstones: a consumable that repairs the weapon or tool in your hands by 25%, away from any workbench. Each metal tier has its own whetstone Forge Comfort 3% increased smelting and charcoal kiln speed per point of comfortSmelters, kilns and forges near you work faster with every point of comfort, the way hives do Fitted Plate 10% increased armour with Smith equipmentCrafting or upgrading heavy armour has a 25% chance to add an item affix that increases its armour. Each eligible mastery rolls independently.

items.title: Mastery options
items.text: Option Effect Inscription Gate You can build the Inscription Gate, a Runecarver portal with pink-violet runes. Shift + use on it opens the map of every portal in the world: pick one and inscribe the link, and everyone who enters the gate steps out there. Azurite Sight Azurite veins within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap: plain, corrupted and divine each with its own icon. A vein mined out by more than three quarters is no longer marked. Divine Touch +2% chance for divine azuriteEach chisel hit on a plain azurite vein outside the mist has a chance to turn it divine, with the same lightning as a heavenly strike. Any chisel works, in any biome. Ascendant Rune +10% chance that a property added by a rune rises one tierWhen a rune adds or raises a property, it has a chance to rise one tier more as a separate step, beyond the item's level limit. You see a second flash, hear a chime and read "+1 affix tier". Perfect Inscription +10% chance that a property rolled by a rune takes the highest value of its tierA property rolled by a rune (Fate included) has a chance to take the highest value of its tier. Portal Crate Away from a workbench, dismantling a portal packs it into a crate that keeps its tag, author, durability and Inscription Gate link. Place it back from the crate anywhere. A crate cannot pass through a portal. Relic Passage Dragon eggs for summoning, Hildir's chests and dvergr parts (charred cogwheels, dvergr needles, mechanical springs) go through portals, with no portal toll. Ore and metal are not included. Vacuum Chest Unlocks the Vacuum Chest at the Rune Carver Table. It takes finished goods from smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills around it and feeds them from its contents. Shift + mouse wheel sets the radius, Shift + E the kind of goods it collects. Chisel Quarrying Rune chisels also mine stone and ore deposits, like a pickaxe of the same metal: bronze, iron or black metal (flametal hits as hard as black metal). A deposit too hard for that pickaxe is too hard for the chisel. Chisel hits do not train the Pickaxes skill. Azurite veins are mined as before.

items.title: Rare affixes
items.text:
Craft notable · Timber · Runecarver · Show on tree

10% increased rune-crafted affix rarity

items.title: Mastery options
items.text: Option Effect Inscription Gate You can build the Inscription Gate, a Runecarver portal with pink-violet runes. Shift + use on it opens the map of every portal in the world: pick one and inscribe the link, and everyone who enters the gate steps out there. Azurite Sight Azurite veins within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap: plain, corrupted and divine each with its own icon. A vein mined out by more than three quarters is no longer marked. Divine Touch +2% chance for divine azuriteEach chisel hit on a plain azurite vein outside the mist has a chance to turn it divine, with the same lightning as a heavenly strike. Any chisel works, in any biome. Ascendant Rune +10% chance that a property added by a rune rises one tierWhen a rune adds or raises a property, it has a chance to rise one tier more as a separate step, beyond the item's level limit. You see a second flash, hear a chime and read "+1 affix tier". Perfect Inscription +10% chance that a property rolled by a rune takes the highest value of its tierA property rolled by a rune (Fate included) has a chance to take the highest value of its tier. Portal Crate Away from a workbench, dismantling a portal packs it into a crate that keeps its tag, author, durability and Inscription Gate link. Place it back from the crate anywhere. A crate cannot pass through a portal. Relic Passage Dragon eggs for summoning, Hildir's chests and dvergr parts (charred cogwheels, dvergr needles, mechanical springs) go through portals, with no portal toll. Ore and metal are not included. Vacuum Chest Unlocks the Vacuum Chest at the Rune Carver Table. It takes finished goods from smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills around it and feeds them from its contents. Shift + mouse wheel sets the radius, Shift + E the kind of goods it collects. Chisel Quarrying Rune chisels also mine stone and ore deposits, like a pickaxe of the same metal: bronze, iron or black metal (flametal hits as hard as black metal). A deposit too hard for that pickaxe is too hard for the chisel. Chisel hits do not train the Pickaxes skill. Azurite veins are mined as before.

items.title: Tanner
items.text: Profession · Beast

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 184 1 5 Fibres gather under a practiced hand, and an extra length of thread winds onto the spool. The same care gives leather gear a lasting life. Hide and wood are measured twice before the knife falls. Nothing useful is left among the offcuts. 631 2 4 Hide and sinew are measured twice by lamplight, and every offcut is saved. The awl flies across coat and bow alike; patient seams and well-seasoned wood make gear fit to endure many winters. 1,887 3 2 Now and then a bow or coat leaves the bench finer than its pattern. Such work is remembered long after its maker. 3,175 4 3 Layers of hide overlap like a beast’s winter coat. Gear from this workshop bends beneath a blow before it breaks. 4,969 5 1 Wheel and needle work as one where the loom never rests. The tanner draws swift thread and wastes neither hide nor timber.

items.title: Beekeeper
items.text: Profession · Mead and Herbs

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 55 1 1 A humble straw skep hums at the meadow's edge. Patient keepers sometimes find a second queen stirring among the comb, ready to found a new hive. 184 2 2 Bees swarm in the warm hour after rain. Keepers who listen to the hive know when a young queen is about to rise from the brood. 547 3 4 Golden comb drips thick in the late summer sun. Honey from these hives fills the jars to the brim and sits heavy and sweet in a hungry belly. 908 4 3 Deep in the clover fields the hives divide and multiply. Each new queen carries the old colony's blessing into another skep. 1,594 5 7 The hives here never seem to sleep. Bees drone from first light to dusk, and the honey flows faster and more freely than elsewhere. 2,215 6 8 Old skeps stand in rows like the halls of a small kingdom. Honey overflows the combs, and young queens rise to rule new swarms. 3,726 8 6 The bees here work as if Odin himself awaits his mead. Comb fills quickly, and the hive repays its keeper sooner than seems natural. 4,969 9 5 At the meadow's heart stands a hive older than any rune-stone, and its bees never rest. Honey runs from it as swiftly as a spring thaw. This honey is said to be gathered from the flowers at Yggdrasil's roots. A single spoonful warms the blood and sustains a warrior through long marches.

items.title: Mead brewer
items.text: Profession · Mead and Herbs

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 55 1 8 A carefully tended barrel gives a little more than expected. The first cellar rewards patience with a fuller horn. 184 2 1 Shelves of oak are built along the cellar wall for more barrels. Tar and oil simmer beside the mead, and they grow keener under a careful hand. 547 3 5 Racks line the dark cellar from floor to ceiling. A brewer who builds well finds room for one more cask, and then one more again. 908 4 4 Rendered fat and pine tar thicken in the brewer's pots. Oils made here burn hotter and keep their bite long after they are bottled. 2,215 6 7 Some batches seem to brew themselves, filling one more bottle than the recipe promised. Oil and mead alike spill over in plenty here. 2,929 7 3 The cellar answers a practiced hand. Mead matures swiftly, and the last measure sometimes fills another horn. 3,726 8 2 Deep in the cellar, oils age in sealed jars until they are dark as bog water. Their potency lasts long after the stopper is pulled. Old brewers whispered runes over each barrel. The mead from this cellar strikes harder, and its blessing lingers long after the horn is emptied. 4,969 9 6 The great vats of the mead hall reek of tar and resin. A master brewer coaxes an extra flask of oil from every pressing.

items.title: Builder
items.text: Profession · Timber

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 122 1 1 Every beam has its place in a rising hall. A sure hand sets the timbers true and turns a humble shelter into a lasting home. 423 2 5 A long arm and a steady hammer reach the highest rafters. Hearths and sconces in a well-made hall burn their fuel slowly. 1,270 3 6 Tar-sealed beams and layered thatch keep the hall dry through storms. Deep joints stand against troll fists and the years; spare pegs never go to waste, and a well-tended bench serves the builder far beyond its walls. 2,126 4 2 Old builders could raise a longhouse from the timber another wasted on a shed. No peg or plank is squandered here. 3,726 5 4 Warm furs, carved pillars and a hearth at the centre. A hall built here welcomes the weary and lets them rest deeper. 4,969 6 3 The master builder walks the walls with a mallet, and cracks close wherever the mending reaches. Whole halls are made whole again in one round.

items.text: Profession · Table

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 122 1 6 A blackened pot over a peat fire, and a cook who never lets it rest. Stews here bubble ready before the hunters are home. A careful cook stretches the pantry and leaves an extra serving by the hearth. 423 2 2 Some pots yield more than went into them, and the meals stay with a warrior longer. A blessed hearth feeds the whole longhouse. 1,270 3 5 Spits turn and griddles hiss in quick succession. The busy cook keeps scraps for the next meal and lets nothing go to waste. 2,126 4 3 Hearty stews of serpent and barley bread fill the belly and keep it full for a long time. Feasts here are remembered for days. 3,726 5 1 Food from this hearth nourishes like a blessing from Frigg. A single bowl sets a warrior's body strong for the long fight. 4,969 6 4 A busy hearth rewards practiced hands. Meals come swiftly, and the table is seldom empty.

items.text: Profession · Road

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 86 1 5 Dusty burial chambers hide more than bones. A relic seeker's eye picks out one more trinket, and the finer pieces glint brighter in the gloom. 306 2 1 Grave goods are scattered in the crypts for those with patience. A careful delver leaves with a heavier sack than most. 908 3 7 Behind a loose stone or under a rotting shield, another treasure waits. Deep delvers rarely leave a crypt with just one find. The barrows give more to those who search every corner. Coin and amber pile higher in the sack of a patient seeker. 1,535 4 3 Old chests in sunken crypts are heavier than they look. Those who know the dead's habits find them packed full to the lid. 2,681 5 4 Jarls were buried with their finest treasures. Delvers who read the old marks pull richer and rarer relics from every chest and corner. 3,726 6 2 A torch in a cold tomb is a hearth of its own. Its light chases away fear and grants rest, even among the restless dead. 4,969 7 6 Deep below the earth, the lantern is life. Old delvers' torches burned brighter and lasted much longer than the dark could wait. In the deepest vaults, treasures lie in heaps beneath the dust. The seeker who reaches this far leaves with a heavier pack. Pitch-soaked rags and a well-trimmed wick. The delver's light reaches further into the dark and refuses to go out.

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 67 1 3 Furrows cut by hand in black earth. A frugal farmer drops each seed with care, and the sack seems to last forever. 233 2 2 Turnips and barley sit lighter on the shoulder after the harvest. Farmers here carry home a full crop without bending double. 688 3 7 Well-tended beds reward careful hands with an extra share of the harvest. 1,155 4 5 Sacks are packed tight and slung just so. The harvest feels lighter on the long walk from the field to the storehouse. 2,029 5 4 Every seed counts on the Plains, where the wind steals what it can. A thrifty sower keeps the pouch full for the next season. 2,826 6 8 Warm rain wakes the rich soil, and practiced hands work long furrows without tiring. Every grain is counted; ripe crops fill the baskets with food and seed, and strong backs bring the heavy harvest home. 3,726 7 6 The great barns of old held more than any single field could fill. A master farmer carries a bountiful harvest from one season's work. 4,969 8 1 At the heart of the fields stands a stone carved with Freyr's rune. Those who sow beneath it lose barely any seed to the earth.

items.title: Fisher
items.text: Profession · Table

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 55 1 8 A quiet pier and a patient angler. The fish here seem to find the hook more readily, and the line reels in smoothly. Nets sometimes pull up more than herring. Old fishers swore the sea gives up lost treasures to those who wait long enough. 184 2 2 Hours at the water's edge with an easy cast. The seasoned angler wastes no breath fighting the line. 547 3 5 Swift hands at the reel bring the catch to shore before it can thrash free. The best fishers haul in fish before the tide turns. 908 4 3 Rich shoals crowd the quiet cove, and a patient angler brings home more than a single catch. Sometimes the deep tide offers stranger gifts: a barnacled chest or a lost amulet glinting beneath the fish. 2,215 6 1 A tight knot keeps the bait on the hook, and an easy cast spares the arm. The patient fisher loses little to the waves. 2,929 7 7 Here the water always seems alive with movement. Fish rise to the hook as if summoned by Njord himself. 3,726 8 6 A well-rested fisher has a calm mind and steady hands. After a night by the fire, the catch comes up in pairs. 4,969 9 4 Beyond the last skerry, the sea holds the wreckage of a thousand longships. Those who fish here pull up treasure as often as cod.

items.title: Forager
items.text: Profession · Mead and Herbs

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 86 1 2 Raspberries in the meadows, mushrooms under the birches. A sharp-eyed forager often finds a second cluster hiding behind the first. 306 2 7 The forest feeds those who know where to look. Baskets fill with extra berries and woven bags hold more of nature's bounty. Wild greens grow back where they were picked, and the forager's hands snatch berries from further away. The woods are generous here. 908 3 4 In the shadow of old pines, mushrooms grow in thick rings. A forager who knows the spot comes back with twice the haul. 1,535 4 5 Picked thistle and bramble sprout anew with unusual haste. Old foragers knew the right way to leave a bush so it would bloom again. 2,681 5 6 A broad sweep of the hand gathers a whole patch at once. Berries and herbs from all around fall into the forager's basket. 3,726 6 1 Deep in the Black Forest, the ground is thick with plenty. Each bush seems to give a little more than it should. 4,969 7 3 Sturdy baskets and deep pouches. The master forager returns from the woods heavily laden with everything the land offers.

items.title: Herder
items.text: Profession · Beast

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 86 1 7 A gentle word and a handful of berries. Boars calm more quickly for a patient herder and stay content long after being fed. 306 2 6 Full troughs and warm straw. Well-fed beasts here are content for long stretches, and the pens grow crowded with young. 908 3 5 Spring comes early to these pens, and the herd grows with it. Boars and wolves raised here are quick to breed. 1,535 4 3 A good meal lasts a long time in a well-kept stable. The beasts graze peacefully, rarely restless with hunger. 2,681 5 4 Old herders had a knack for feeding a lox until its belly stayed full for days. The beasts in this valley never go hungry. 3,726 6 2 The great herds of the Plains were raised here, generation after generation. The pens are never empty of young. 4,969 7 1 Even the wildest lox and the fiercest wolf bow before a herder of legend. Taming here takes but a moment of patience.

items.title: Hunter
items.text: Profession · Beast

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 86 1 2 Feathers and flint by the fire. Sometimes the hunter finishes the evening with a few more arrows than were planned. 306 2 1 Arrows fletched quickly and quivers stuffed full. A busy hunter's camp turns out shafts by the bundle. 908 3 5 A patient hunter gathers a richer bounty from every hunt. Nothing useful is left behind in the grass. 1,535 4 3 A silent step carries farther than a hurried chase. The forest hears little as the hunter passes. 2,681 5 6 Deer fall in the meadows, and the hunter's pack is deep enough to carry them all. The forest provides generously here. 3,726 6 4 The hunter's quiver never seems to empty, and the kill yields more than expected. Ravens follow these trails eagerly. 4,969 7 7 A master hunter moves unseen and carries the weight of the kill as if it were nothing. The forest falls silent as the hunter passes.

items.title: Miner
items.text: Profession · Forge

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 184 2 2 The rock's weakness grows wider beneath a practised eye. Copper splits easily where the seam is struck true. Weak seams show themselves more often here, and the miner's back is spared the weight of the ore. Hauling bog iron is less of a burden. Stone is not a solid mass. Old miners tapped the rock and listened for the cracks that hinted where it might yield. 908 4 7 The pick strikes swiftly in a tireless rhythm. A seasoned miner leaves the rock face with a heavier load upon their back. 1,594 5 1 A sharp strike to the heart of the vein can shatter a rock that might have taken ages to break. The blow spreads through the stone. 2,215 6 3 Sometimes a whole vein shatters at once, raining ore across the cave floor. The Dvergr of the Mistlands called this the gift of the deep. 2,929 7 8 Weak seams hold their shape longer under the lamp. Silver from the mountain feels lighter in the miner's pack. 2,940 1 6 A pick loosens an extra fragment from the vein. A sturdy pack and a steady back carry the mountain’s bounty home. 3,726 8 4 The mountain's heart yields to heavy blows. Each strike tears more ore loose than the last. 4,969 9 5 At the roots of the world, where the Dvergr once delved, cracks open all over the stone. Old masters could see every flaw in the vein.

items.title: Pathfinder
items.text: Profession · Road

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 55 1 1 A wayfarer's first lessons: leap without tiring, swim without drowning. Rivers and stones barely slow the path ahead. 184 2 2 A crackling campfire under the open sky. A wanderer finds true rest by its warmth, far from any hall. 547 3 8 Light boots and a long stride. Swift travellers cover the leagues between the meadows and the mountains before nightfall. Smoke rises from a ring of stones beside the trail. A seasoned traveller makes the wild a home with a single fire. 908 4 4 Stories by the fire and a pelt to sleep on. The road is long, but the wayfarer's camps grant a comfort like that of a mead hall. 2,215 6 3 A fall from a cliff is but a stumble to a seasoned wayfarer. And when death comes, the path back to the corpse is run with renewed vigour. Swift legs and a lofty leap carry the wayfarer over hill and stream. With each journey, the unknown map unfolds a little wider. 2,929 7 7 Old runes etched in stones and ruins call out from afar. Experienced travellers can sense their glow long before they reach them. 3,726 8 6 From every ridge, the wayfarer sees for miles. The fog of uncharted lands melts away before a wise traveller's gaze. 4,969 9 5 Even Valhalla's gate cannot hold back a true wayfarer. After death, they race back to reclaim their gear, swift and fearless.

The runecarver's lore begins to stir beneath the fog. 2,940 1 2 At the heart of the carvers' hall, a great stone hums with old power. Its runes were cut when Yggdrasil was young. 2,940 1 3 Runes burned into iron and bone. The carver's craft reaches into deeper mysteries, where wisdom costs dearly. 2,940 1 4 The marks of the Allfather himself are said to be traced on these walls. Few carvers dare to read them aloud. 2,940 1 5 A rune-stone half sunk in the moss, its carvings still sharp. Some of the old carvers' knowledge survives here. 2,940 1 6 Futhark letters glow faintly in the lamplight. Old carvers knew which runes bind and which unleash.

items.text: Profession · Timber

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 55 1 6 Oak ribs and pine planks promise a voyage with a full hold. A shipwright bears the supplies with ease and shapes hulls that cut swiftly through the waves. 184 2 8 Taut sails catch the wind while a well-shaped keel answers every touch of the helm. Ships raised in this yard run swift and turn sure; from the prow, a watchful sailor finds distant shores and a safe way through the waves. 547 3 3 Many voyages teach the feel of the sea. The skilled helmsman catches every breath of wind and steers through narrow straits with ease. 908 4 7 An old boathouse lies shrouded in mist. The secrets of the shipwrights who built here are known only to the tides. 1,594 5 1 Sailors whisper prayers to Njord before the voyage. On these waters, the wind so often blows from behind. 2,929 7 2 Fast ships and strong swimmers. Those who fall from the deck reach the hull again without tiring. 3,726 8 4 In the far Ocean, a lookout's eyes can see beyond the horizon. Sailors who dive near their ship swim tirelessly, and the sea gives up more. 4,969 9 5 The great drakkars of legend were built from the timber of a single ancient oak. Master shipwrights waste nothing in their work.

items.title: Woodcutter
items.text: Profession · Timber

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 55 1 1 Every measured swing follows the grain. The axe keeps its rhythm while timber falls in steady piles. 184 2 7 A steady axe coaxes an extra log from the trunk. With the timber piled high, a well-handled cart carries the harvest home. When a great tree falls, it crushes all beneath it. Lumberjacks here know how to make every blow and every fall count. A keen edge finds the perfect cut. Sometimes a single swing splits the trunk deeper than ten others could. 547 3 8 Old pines crash down with the force of a giant's fist. The ground shakes when the lumberjack's work is done. A heavy blade and a mighty swing. Trees fall faster and harder in this part of the forest. The axe finds the heartwood with a single, perfect blow. Lumberjacks here strike where the grain is weakest. 908 4 6 A grove of ancient trees, shrouded in fog. The lumberjacks who worked here left behind tales and tools of an unknown craft. 1,594 5 5 Every tree here gives more than its share. Logs pile up quickly, and the woodpile grows tall by evening. 2,215 6 3 Strong shoulders and a sturdy pack. The lumberjack carries home a heavy load of timber as if it were kindling. One mighty swing cleaves through several trunks at once. The forest thins quickly before a master lumberjack's axe. 3,726 8 4 Steady hands keep the rhythm unbroken, one blow flowing into the next. items.title: Aftershock
items.text: A second eruption at a slam's point a moment later, with the slam's own damage and its own modifiers. It is rolled once per slam, not per enemy hit, and never makes another aftershock.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Slam: Valheim's area attacks (the sledge's swing and others like it) count, and so does an alternative attack Ground Strike turns into one: it uses the weapon's own area radius, or 3 m if the weapon has no area attack. Your area of effect widens a slam's radius.

Aftershock: rolled once per slam, at most 100%. 0.45 s later it erupts at the slam's point, in the slam's radius × the area increases that only apply to aftershocks, and hits everything there with the slam's full damage. An aftershock never rolls another, though repeat chance can make it erupt once more.

An aftershock pushes enemies away from where it erupts.

A thrown club, mace or sledge that lands on the ground (not on a creature) slams there once: 3 m × your area of effect, with 100% of the weapon's damage × your skill multiplier, against every enemy and object in it. A thrown sceptre that lands casts its spell there instead.

A charged attack that isn't a slam can make aftershocks too, from aftershock chance that works with charged attacks: each full 100% gives one, and the rest is a chance for one more, each 0.45 s after the last, where the enemy was hit.

Primary attacks that are slams: Demolisher, Frostfire Sledge, Iron Sledge, Nord Sledge, Stagbreaker, Thunderblood Sledge, Wooden Sledge.

Alternative attacks that Ground Strike turns into slams: Battleaxe, Berserkir Axes, Black Metal Atgeir, Black Metal Battleaxe, Bleeding Berserkir Axes, Bronze Atgeir, Brutal Slayer, Crystal Battleaxe, Demolisher, Early Axes, Frostfire Atgeir, Frostfire Greataxe, Frostfire Greatsword, Frostfire Sledge, Himminafl, Iron Atgeir, Iron Sledge, Krom, Nord Atgeir, Nord Greataxe, Nord Greatsword, Nord Sledge, Primal Berserkir Axes, Primal Slayer, Scourging Slayer, Skull Splittur, Slayer, Stagbreaker, Thunderblood Atgeir, Thunderblood Greataxe, Thunderblood Greatsword, Thunderblood Sledge, Thundering Berserkir Axes, Wooden Atgeir, Wooden Battleaxe, Wooden Greatsword, Wooden Sledge.

items.title: Ailment damage
items.text: Increases damage over time from bleeding, burning and poison, separately from the damage of the hit that caused them. It does not affect chill. Old shock-damage bonuses now act as shock effect.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Ailment gauge: bleeding, burning, poison, chill and shock each fill their own on the enemy, from the matching part of your hits' damage as the enemy takes it, after its resistances and armour: slash, fire, poison, frost and lightning.

gauge filled by a hit = matching damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up)

How much of the gauge one hit fills, by its damage as a share of the enemy's base health (its maximum health without the mod's difficulty scaling):

Damage ÷ base health 5% 10% 25% 50% Filled, +0% build-up 8% 16% 40% 80% Filled, +100% build-up 16% 32% 80% 100%

At 100% the ailment starts, from the strongest matching hit since the gauge began to fill. The gauge then stays full, so every further matching hit applies the ailment again from its own damage. 3 s after the last matching hit the gauge drains, 25% per second. Chill ends when it is empty (at most 7 s after that hit); the other ailments run their own time.

What each ailment does with that damage:

  • Bleeding: 20% of the slash damage per second for 4 s (80% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (physical). Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One bleed per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second.
  • Burning: 25% of the fire damage per second for 4 s (100% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (fire); fire damage increases don't apply again. Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One burn per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second. A wet enemy burns out 6 times as fast.
  • Poison: 15% of the poison damage per second for 4 s (60% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (poison), plus any share of the enemy's base health your stats add, spread over the same 4 s (ailment damage doesn't raise that part). Longer duration adds seconds. Each player can keep 3 poisons on an enemy (more with limit bonuses); past that, a new one replaces your weakest if it would deal more. Skeletons and the Charred take poison damage normally, but their poison gauge fills at half speed; summoned skeletons stay immune.
  • Chill: Valheim's frost effect, its strength × (1 + your general and chill ailment damage increases); ailment and status duration make it last longer.

  • Shock: for 3 s the enemy takes more damage from every source and builds up stagger faster, by the shock's strength. Only the strongest shock on an enemy acts, whoever applied it. Flat ailment damage does nothing for shock.

    shock strength = 0.5 × (lightning damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health))^0.4 × (1 + shock effect increases) × more, at most 50%; under 5%, no shock

    The lightning damage here is the hit's, before the enemy's resistances and armour.

Ailment damage multipliers for burning, poison and bleeding: × (1 + ailment damage increases, general and that ailment's) × their more multipliers; flat ailment damage adds its amount spread over 4 s. Each player's ailments tick on their own, once a second.

  • Burning: 25% of the fire damage per second for 4 s (100% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (fire); fire damage increases don't apply again. Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One burn per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second. A wet enemy burns out 6 times as fast.
  • Poison: 15% of the poison damage per second for 4 s (60% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (poison), plus any share of the enemy's base health your stats add, spread over the same 4 s (ailment damage doesn't raise that part). Longer duration adds seconds. Each player can keep 3 poisons on an enemy (more with limit bonuses); past that, a new one replaces your weakest if it would deal more. Skeletons and the Charred take poison damage normally, but their poison gauge fills at half speed; summoned skeletons stay immune.
  • Chill: Valheim's frost effect, its strength × (1 + your general and chill ailment damage increases); ailment and status duration make it last longer.

  • Shock: for 3 s the enemy takes more damage from every source and builds up stagger faster, by the shock's strength. Only the strongest shock on an enemy acts, whoever applied it. Flat ailment damage does nothing for shock.

    shock strength = 0.5 × (lightning damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health))^0.4 × (1 + shock effect increases) × more, at most 50%; under 5%, no shock

    The lightning damage here is the hit's, before the enemy's resistances and armour.

Ailment damage multipliers for burning, poison and bleeding: × (1 + ailment damage increases, general and that ailment's) × their more multipliers; flat ailment damage adds its amount spread over 4 s. Each player's ailments tick on their own, once a second.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Area of effect
items.text: Increases the size or reach of supported attacks and effects. It does not increase their damage; area damage is separate.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Area of effect widens attacks in a straight line: the factor multiplies the hit radius, not the ground it covers. +100% area doubles the radius and covers four times the ground.

radius × max(0.1, (1 + area increases) × area multipliers)

Area attacks (a slam is one) get the wider radius; other swings reach further as well.

items.title: Armour
items.text: Reduces damage remaining after rune shield and block. It absorbs a greater share of smaller hits; armour penetration ignores part of this protection.

items.title: Armour
items.text:
Armour is Valheim's own: it reduces each hit by the same share for all its damage types, much against small hits, less against big ones. With hit damage the sum of the hit's damage types:

armour < damage ÷ 2: damage taken = damage − armour; otherwise: damage taken = damage² ÷ (4 × armour) armour against creatures = your armour × 1.05 − the creature's armour penetration

Armour applies after rune shield and block. Creatures ignore part of it: see enemy penetration. Damage taken, by armour and hit:

items.title: Attributes
items.text: Strength supports health and carry weight; Dexterity supports stamina and its regeneration; Intelligence supports eitr and rune shield. Governing attributes also raise weapon damage through the skill multiplier.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Each point of an attribute gives:

Attribute Per point Per 100 points Strength 0.125% increased health regeneration+0.2 carry weight 12.5% increased health regeneration+20 carry weight Dexterity 0.185% increased stamina regeneration0.2% increased evasion rating 18.5% increased stamina regeneration20% increased evasion rating Intelligence 0.185% increased eitr regeneration+0.16 rune shield 18.5% increased eitr regeneration+16 rune shield

Weapons governed by attributes multiply their damage by a random skill multiplier, picked anew for every hit between its midpoint − 0.15 and + 0.15, never below 0. The midpoint grows with the weapon's governing attribute points (with two, their average); Valheim's own weapon skill level doesn't count.

midpoint = 0.4 × (1 + 1.5 × (points ÷ 300)^0.75) Points 0 50 100 200 300 500 Midpoint 0.4 0.56 0.66 0.84 1 1.28

Governing attributes by weapon skill:

Weapon skill Governing attributes Swords Strength, Intelligence Knives Intelligence, Dexterity Clubs Strength Polearms Strength, Intelligence Spears Dexterity, Strength Axes Dexterity, Strength Bows Dexterity Elemental Magic Intelligence Blood Magic Intelligence Fists Dexterity Pickaxes Strength Crossbows Dexterity, Strength

Sceptres are governed by Strength and Intelligence, whatever their skill.

With Shifted Requirements, 50% of your Strength also counts as Dexterity for two-handed weapons and bows (not fist weapons).

items.title: Backstab
items.text: Extra damage against an enemy that has not noticed the attacker yet, regardless of attack direction. Weapons carry no backstab bonus of their own: it comes only from sneak attack damage bonuses.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
When the hit reaches an enemy, the increases that depend on it join the same sum:

  • increases against enemies of a kind or in a state (bosses, enemies with ailments and the like)
  • backstab: against an enemy that hasn't noticed you; Valheim's own backstab bonus is turned off
  • +15% while the enemy is staggered, instead of Valheim's double damage (stagger)
  • charged attack: +25%

Flat damage against the enemy (flat backstab damage, flat damage against enemies of a kind) goes to the hit's largest type, × your skill multiplier × (1 + the whole sum). It comes after the critical hit, so a crit doesn't multiply it.

Last come the increases and more multipliers that need something of the hit and something of the enemy together; the increases join the same sum.

Every step of a hit, in order: Order of a hit.

items.title: Biome level
items.text: Experience from a biome decreases as the character outlevels it. This depends on the biome rather than the enemy; direct passive-point rewards are unaffected.

items.title: Area levels
items.text:
Every biome has a fixed level. A creature's level is the level of the biome it stands in (stars don't change it): it sets the creature's accuracy and the item level of its loot, a chest takes the level of its biome, and gear bought from a trader the level of the biome the trader is in. It doesn't scale health or damage, except for the monolith bosses. With the Raid level scaling setting (off by default, on in Merciless), raiders take the level of the biome the raid comes from, and scale with it. Each biome also has a recommended player level: up to the next biome's, it gives full experience; past it, experience falls off.

A creature in the Blight Mist takes the level of the next boss's biome by the world's progress (the first boss not yet defeated; the Deep North once Fader is), wherever it stands.

Biome Level Full experience up to level Meadows 1 19 Black Forest 19 43 Swamp 43 77 Mountain 77 97 Plains 97 130 Mistlands 130 181 Ashlands 181 246 Deep North 246 311

With the other mechanics: Experience and levels.

items.title: Experience fall-off
items.text:
Past a biome's recommended range, the combat experience you gain there fades. The ranges follow the recommended player levels (a server setting, by default the biomes' levels). The level that counts is yours; the biome is where the creature dies (for kills) or where you stand (for hits). Being below a biome's level costs nothing.

kept = max(0.05, 0.05 ^ (levels past the range ÷ 10))

Experience fades to 5% at 10 levels past the range, and never lower:

items.title: Bleeding
items.text: Slash damage fills the bleeding gauge. When it fills, bleeding deals 20% of the slash damage of the strongest hit in the build-up per second for 4 s, over time and through armour. Bleeding damage, the damage over time multiplier and duration change it separately. Each player keeps their own strongest bleed on a target; a weaker one does not refresh it.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Bleeding builds up on the enemy's ailment gauge from slash damage as the enemy takes it, after its resistances and armour.

gauge filled by a hit = slash damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up)

At 100% the ailment starts, from the strongest matching hit since the gauge began to fill. The gauge then stays full, so every further matching hit applies the ailment again from its own damage. 3 s after the last matching hit the gauge drains, 25% per second. Chill ends when it is empty (at most 7 s after that hit); the other ailments run their own time.

What it does: 20% of the slash damage per second for 4 s (80% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (physical). Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One bleed per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second.

Ailment damage multipliers for burning, poison and bleeding: × (1 + ailment damage increases, general and that ailment's) × their more multipliers; flat ailment damage adds its amount spread over 4 s. Each player's ailments tick on their own, once a second.

items.title: Block
items.text: Block power absorbs part or all of an incoming hit; remaining damage passes through. Blocking spends stamina according to the strength of the hit.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Block: when you block a hit from the front, Valheim treats your block power like armour against the whole hit, every damage type, after the blocking item's own resistances.

block power = max(0, Valheim's block power × (1 + the shield's own block power increases) + flat block power) × (1 + block power increases) Valheim's block power = the item's block power at its quality × (1 + Blocking skill × 0.5) parry: block power × the item's parry bonus × (1 + parry bonus increases)

A parry is a block within 0.25 s of raising your guard, with an item that has a parry bonus. A block costs Valheim's block stamina × the share of your block power the hit used; a parry costs a fixed amount.

What gets through works like armour: block power under half the hit takes that much off; more than that cuts the hit to hit² ÷ (4 × block power). The rest goes on to your armour and rune shield.

If you're out of stamina, or the blocked hit's stagger breaks your guard, nothing is blocked. A hit that meets your block can't be a Glancing Blow.

items.title: Blunt damage
items.text: A physical damage type that builds armour break. Stagger uses the hit's separate stagger power.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
All the increased and reduced damage that applies to a hit is added into one sum, and the hit is multiplied by 1 + that sum once: general damage, your weapon kind's, melee, ranged or spell damage, attacks', alternative attacks', that of hits that aren't projectiles, a running attack's bonus, and the increases that depend on the enemy (below).

A scepter's hits count as the kind of attack they are: its spells take spell damage increases, its other attacks melee or ranged ones.

damage of a type = (weapon damage × skill multiplier + oils + flat damage × skill multiplier) × (1 + increases + that type's increases)

Each damage type adds its own increases to the sum, for that type only: fire, frost and lightning also add elemental damage increases, and slash, pierce and blunt add physical damage increases. So +50% damage and +50% fire damage make fire damage × 2, not × 2.25.

Projectiles: projectile damage increases join the sum too, with the projectile speed increases any of your stats turn into damage, and so do a torch's damage increases.

Bows and crossbows split each shot in two parts. The ammo's share is its damage ÷ (the weapon's damage + the ammo's). That part takes the sum without your bow or crossbow damage increases, plus your projectile damage increases (bow or crossbow projectile ones included); the weapon's part takes the sum as it is, without projectile increases.

damage = weapon's part × (1 + sum) + ammo's part × (1 + sum − bow or crossbow increases + projectile increases)

Chopping and mining: increases against trees, ore and resources join the same sum, and so flat damage against them grows with the whole sum.

Every step of a hit, in order: Order of a hit.

items.title: Burning
items.text: Fire damage fills the burning gauge. When it fills, burning deals 25% of the fire damage of the strongest hit in the build-up per second for 4 s, as fire damage over time. Burning damage and the damage over time multiplier make it stronger, duration makes it last longer. Each player keeps their own strongest burn on a target; a weaker one does not refresh it. Wet shortens it, and chill removes it.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Burning builds up on the enemy's ailment gauge from fire damage as the enemy takes it, after its resistances and armour.

gauge filled by a hit = fire damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up)

At 100% the ailment starts, from the strongest matching hit since the gauge began to fill. The gauge then stays full, so every further matching hit applies the ailment again from its own damage. 3 s after the last matching hit the gauge drains, 25% per second. Chill ends when it is empty (at most 7 s after that hit); the other ailments run their own time.

What it does: 25% of the fire damage per second for 4 s (100% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (fire); fire damage increases don't apply again. Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One burn per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second. A wet enemy burns out 6 times as fast.

Ailment damage multipliers for burning, poison and bleeding: × (1 + ailment damage increases, general and that ailment's) × their more multipliers; flat ailment damage adds its amount spread over 4 s. Each player's ailments tick on their own, once a second.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Burning Ground
items.text: Deals fire damage over time and builds burning through its explicit ailment channel. Spells create it when they hit terrain if you have the corresponding source. Identical overlapping ground does not stack.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Ground Effects: a passive that creates ground for a damage type (Ashen Wake, Blighted Soil, Glassbound, Stormbed) makes your spells leave a patch where they land: a projectile that hits the ground or an object (not one that hits an enemy), or an area spell where it strikes. One impact makes one patch, with a layer for each of the spell's fire, frost, lightning and poison damage that has such a passive.

Each layer comes from the spell's damage of its type, after your damage increases (ground damage increases join them) and before its critical strike:

damage per second = 20% × that damage × your damage over time multiplier for the type build-up per second = 20% × that damage, into burning, chill, shock or poison

A patch has a radius of 2 m × (1 + area increases; a spell's patch also takes spell area increases), at most 12 m, and lasts 4 s × (1 + effect duration increases), at most 60 s.

Enemies standing on it (on the ground, not swimming) take its damage every 0.2 s, paid about once a second, through their resistances. Ground damage is never a critical strike, can't be blocked or evaded, and doesn't stagger. Each enemy takes only the strongest patch of each type, whoever made it; different types add up. Your allies and you take no damage from your patches.

You can keep 1 patch at once (limits); a new one past the limit removes your oldest. Only spell patches count.

Chilled Ground makes everyone on it slide, you and your allies too. It doesn't lower speed: speeding up and braking work at 15% of the usual rate, turning at 35%.

Passives that work while you stand on a kind of ground count any patch of that type, yours or not.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Charged attack
items.text: A charge empowers your next released weapon attack and is consumed even on a miss. Charges do not stack or expire. A charge source can charge the attack again only after its cooldown: 2 s, a critical hit 0.2 s, counted from the last successful charge. A perfect dodge ignores the cooldown and always charges the attack if a dodge roll charges it for you. Spending a charge does not restart cooldowns, and failed grants do not extend them. All hits and projectiles of the released attack share its charge. Spells can consume it only with Charged Casts. The charge itself grants 25% increased damage; charged-attack nodes add further bonuses.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Charged attack: something charges your next weapon attack, and the next melee or ranged attack you release spends it, hit or miss (spells only with ChargeApplicability). One charge waits at a time; it doesn't stack or expire.

charged attack: + 25% increased damage, added to your other damage increases, and rows that work with charged attacks apply

A source charges again only 2 s after it last charged the attack (critical hits: 0.2 s). After any charge, every source also waits the shorter of its own cooldown and 3 s (cut by cooldown recovery). A perfect dodge ignores both cooldowns, but can't charge an attack that's already charged.

What charges the attack. Each source needs the passive or mastery option that grants it:

Charges the attack when Granted by an alternative attack hits an enemy Second edge you activate a trinket Flash Response you cast a spell Spell Primes the Strike you cover 25 m running on the ground or levitating, while no charge waits Giant's Run-Up you jump Leap Before the Blow you land a critical hit with an attack Critical Charge you parry a hit Ready Answer you start a dodge roll (a perfect dodge charges it even on cooldown) Rolling Charge

With Choose the Spend, only alternative attacks spend the charge; with Alternate Leads, alternative attacks don't spend it.

Unbound Charge: rolled once when the charge is spent. On success the attack gets 50% increased damage instead, and every row that works with charged attacks counts twice.

Hit splash: a charged attack's first hit on an enemy also hits every other enemy within 3 m × (1 + area of effect increases), for your splash share of its damage.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.
