items.title: Divine Azurite
items.text:
Materials

A golden radiance runs through the stone, as if a god had touched it.

items.title: Mining
items.text:
Starts appearing in the Swamp: the first time you come within 30 m of a plain azurite vein, a heavenly strike can turn it divine. Chance by biome: Swamp, Mountain: 5%; Plains, Mistlands, Ashlands, Deep North: 10%. In the Plains, Mistlands, Ashlands, Deep North it is certain after 9 misses in a row. Not inside a Blight Mist.

The craft mastery Divine Touch can also turn a plain vein divine while you cut it.

Needs a rune chisel of this tier or higher: Bronze Rune Chisel / Iron Rune Chisel / Black Metal Rune Chisel / Flametal Rune Chisel. Pickaxes can't cut azurite veins.

These veins are ×2.5 as hard to cut as plain ones.

items.title: Eye Between Worlds
items.text:
Unique jewel

Limit: 1

items.title: Lines
items.text:
• Gazes through the worlds to a random knowledge portal, and the way opens

Not every road runs between two steps.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
When it drops, its line points at one of the tree's portals, picked at random:

  • The Eastern Rift · Show on tree (normally revealed only to the Runereader ascendancy class)
  • The Western Rift · Show on tree (normally revealed only to the Runereader ascendancy class)
  • The Southern Rift · Show on tree (normally revealed only to the Runereader ascendancy class)

Socketed in an allocated socket (once identified), it turns the hidden node beside the socket into a portal, the Rift of the Eye. Like every portal, the rift connects to all the others, so the path can go on from there. The portal it points at is revealed too, even without its ascendancy class. Take the jewel out and the rift closes; that portal is unallocated again if it would be hidden.

items.title: Drops
items.text:
Drops in rune monolith events (not corrupted ones): from their defenders, and with a 5% chance when you win one.

Dismantling it gives divine and azurite dust by its item level: see Dismantling unique jewels.

items.title: Crossbows
items.text:
Every item of this type that can have properties, and the passives that work with it. All item bases: Item bases.

Crossbows have a magazine: additional projectiles become loaded bolts, and additional projectile chance is rolled once when a reload finishes. Each shot fires one bolt; holding the attack keeps firing at the fire rate, based on the crossbow's own reload time. A saved bolt keeps both the ammunition and the loaded shot.

items.title: Combat and building
items.text:
Critical strikes, evasion, resistances, what creatures pierce, and building costs.

Numbers are the defaults of the Normal difficulty; servers can change them. Every formula here is checked against the mod's code with each patch.

items.title: Attributes
items.text:
Each point of an attribute gives:

Attribute Per point Per 100 points Strength 0.125% increased health regeneration+0.2 carry weight 12.5% increased health regeneration+20 carry weight Dexterity 0.185% increased stamina regeneration0.2% increased evasion rating 18.5% increased stamina regeneration20% increased evasion rating Intelligence 0.185% increased eitr regeneration+0.16 rune shield 18.5% increased eitr regeneration+16 rune shield

Weapons governed by attributes multiply their damage by a random skill multiplier, picked anew for every hit between its midpoint − 0.15 and + 0.15, never below 0. The midpoint grows with the weapon's governing attribute points (with two, their average); Valheim's own weapon skill level doesn't count.

midpoint = 0.4 × (1 + 1.5 × (points ÷ 300)^0.75) Points 0 50 100 200 300 500 Midpoint 0.4 0.56 0.66 0.84 1 1.28

Governing attributes by weapon skill:

Weapon skill Governing attributes Swords Strength, Intelligence Knives Intelligence, Dexterity Clubs Strength Polearms Strength, Intelligence Spears Dexterity, Strength Axes Dexterity, Strength Bows Dexterity Elemental Magic Intelligence Blood Magic Intelligence Fists Dexterity Pickaxes Strength Crossbows Dexterity, Strength

Sceptres are governed by Strength and Intelligence, whatever their skill.

With Shifted Requirements, 50% of your Strength also counts as Dexterity for two-handed weapons and bows (not fist weapons).

items.title: Order of a hit
items.text:
Every hit of yours, weapon or spell, goes through these steps in this order. Increases all go into one sum wherever they come from, so their place changes nothing; the places of flat damage and multipliers do matter.

When you make the hit

  1. Valheim's damage of the weapon at its quality, × the attack's own multiplier (a combo's last hit and the like) × your skill multiplier.
  2. Weapon oils add their damage.
  3. Flat damage, × the skill multiplier.
  4. Conversion, then damage gained as extra.
  5. Increases: × (1 + their sum), each damage type with its own.
  6. Bows and crossbows: the ammo's share of the damage swaps your bow or crossbow damage increases for projectile damage increases.
  7. More multipliers, one after another, rage last.
  8. More projectiles damage.

When it reaches the enemy

  1. Critical strike damage: × its multiplier, on the whole hit.
  2. Bows and crossbows: effective range, × its factor.
  3. Increases against the enemy join the sum; then flat damage against the enemy, which the crit doesn't multiply.
  4. Increases and more multipliers that need the hit and the enemy together.
  5. Armour break adds to the hit's physical damage, and impale multiplies it.
  6. Valheim applies the creature's resistances, with your penetration for fire, frost, lightning and poison.

So flat damage grows with every increase and multiplier after it, increases only add to each other, and a critical strike multiplies everything except flat damage against the enemy.

items.title: Hit damage
items.text: A hit's damage is built in the parts below; Order of a hit lists them in the order they happen.

items.title: Flat damage
items.text:
Flat damage is added before any increase, × your skill multiplier (the same one the weapon's own damage gets). Where it goes:

  • general flat damage, and flat damage for the kind of hit (your weapon kind, melee, spells, projectiles, attacks, alternative attacks and the like): to the hit's largest damage type
  • flat physical damage: to the largest of slash, pierce and blunt (blunt if the hit has none)
  • flat slash, pierce or blunt damage: only to a hit that already has that type
  • flat fire, frost, lightning, poison or spirit damage: always, as that type
  • flat elemental damage: to the largest of the hit's fire, frost and lightning, only if it has one of them

Weapon oils add their damage type before flat damage, without the skill multiplier.

A hit with no damage at all gets neither oils nor flat damage.

items.title: Conversion
items.text:
Damage conversion turns part of a hit's slash, pierce and blunt damage into another type, after flat damage and before increases; no other type converts. Each of the three converts by its own conversions plus those of all physical damage; if they come to more than 100%, they're scaled down to 100% together.

Conversion that depends on the enemy (against bosses, enemies with ailments and the like) counts too.

converted = slash, pierce or blunt × its conversion to the new type, all its conversions together at most 100%

Converted damage is its new type for resistances and ailments, but it grows with the increases of both types: its old type's and its new type's, added together.

Damage gained as extra: worked out from the slash, pierce and blunt damage before conversion, and added after it as its new type. It grows with its new type's increases only.

items.title: Increases
items.text:
All the increased and reduced damage that applies to a hit is added into one sum, and the hit is multiplied by 1 + that sum once: general damage, your weapon kind's, melee, ranged or spell damage, attacks', alternative attacks', that of hits that aren't projectiles, a running attack's bonus, and the increases that depend on the enemy (below).

A scepter's hits count as the kind of attack they are: its spells take spell damage increases, its other attacks melee or ranged ones.

damage of a type = (weapon damage × skill multiplier + oils + flat damage × skill multiplier) × (1 + increases + that type's increases)

Each damage type adds its own increases to the sum, for that type only: fire, frost and lightning also add elemental damage increases, and slash, pierce and blunt add physical damage increases. So +50% damage and +50% fire damage make fire damage × 2, not × 2.25.

Projectiles: projectile damage increases join the sum too, with the projectile speed increases any of your stats turn into damage, and so do a torch's damage increases.

Bows and crossbows split each shot in two parts. The ammo's share is its damage ÷ (the weapon's damage + the ammo's). That part takes the sum without your bow or crossbow damage increases, plus your projectile damage increases (bow or crossbow projectile ones included); the weapon's part takes the sum as it is, without projectile increases.

damage = weapon's part × (1 + sum) + ammo's part × (1 + sum − bow or crossbow increases + projectile increases)

Chopping and mining: increases against trees, ore and resources join the same sum, and so flat damage against them grows with the whole sum.

items.title: More multipliers
items.text:
More (and less) damage multiplies the hit separately, each multiplier after the other: more damage and more damage for your weapon kind, then rage: × (1 + 1% per point × (1 + rage effect increases)), not on spells.

More (and less) projectile damage then multiplies projectiles on its own.

items.title: Against the enemy
items.text:
When the hit reaches an enemy, the increases that depend on it join the same sum:

  • increases against enemies of a kind or in a state (bosses, enemies with ailments and the like)
  • backstab: against an enemy that hasn't noticed you; Valheim's own backstab bonus is turned off
  • +15% while the enemy is staggered, instead of Valheim's double damage (stagger)
  • charged attack: +25%

Flat damage against the enemy (flat backstab damage, flat damage against enemies of a kind) goes to the hit's largest type, × your skill multiplier × (1 + the whole sum). It comes after the critical hit, so a crit doesn't multiply it.

Last come the increases and more multipliers that need something of the hit and something of the enemy together; the increases join the same sum.

items.title: Effective range
items.text:
Effective Range: a bow or crossbow shot deals full damage up to a start distance from where it was shot, then less the further it flies, down to × 0.2 at an end distance and beyond: 14 m and 40 m for bows, 6 m and 30 m for crossbows. Thrown weapons and spells don't fall off.

damage factor = 1 − (distance − start) ÷ (end − start) × 0.8, between × 0.2 and × 1; start and end × range

Range is 1 + your shooting effective range increases (bow or crossbow ones count for that weapon), so +50% puts both distances 1.5 times as far. The factor multiplies the hit when it reaches the enemy, after the critical strike; flat damage against the enemy is added after it and isn't reduced.

For scale: a Wood Floor 2x2 is 2 m on a side, so a bow's 14 m and 40 m are 7 and 20 floors in a row, a crossbow's 6 m and 30 m 3 and 15.

items.title: Crossbow magazine
items.text:
Crossbows shoot from a magazine. Each reload (Valheim's reload, shortened by reload speed) fills it:

[loaded bolts](../glossary/loaded-bolts.md) = ⌊(1 + flat loaded bolts + additional projectiles + ⌊additional projectile chance⌋, +1 with the chance of what is left) × (1 + loaded bolt increases) × more⌋, rolled when the reload finishes time between shots = the crossbow's reload time × 0.2857 ÷ ((1 + [crossbow fire rate](../glossary/crossbow-fire-rate.md) increases) × more)

Each shot fires one bolt and uses one loaded shot; a shot that saves its ammo keeps it. When the magazine is empty, the crossbow reloads; the Reload key (R by default) reloads early whenever the magazine isn't full. The first shot after a reload and the last loaded shot are magazine shots: bonuses can name them.

Critical damage increases for the last loaded shot change how its critical strike multiplier is built.

Crossbow Reload time Between shots Shots per second Arbalest 3.5 s 1 s 1 Frostfire Crossbow 3.5 s 1 s 1 Nord Crossbow 3.5 s 1 s 1 Ripper 3.5 s 1 s 1 Root Ripper 3.5 s 1 s 1 Storm Ripper 3.5 s 1 s 1 Thunderblood Crossbow 3.5 s 1 s 1 Wound Ripper 3.5 s 1 s 1

items.title: Your penetration
items.text:
Valheim gives each creature a step of resistance against each damage type. Your resistance penetration against fire, frost, lightning and poison (elemental penetration counts for the first three) adds to the share of the damage that gets through:

damage dealt = damage × max(0, 1 − resistance + penetration) Creature's step Resistance Damage dealt With 10% penetration With 25% penetration With 50% penetration Very weak -100% 200% 210% 225% 250% Weak -50% 150% 160% 175% 200% Slightly weak -25% 125% 135% 150% 175% Normal 0% 100% 110% 125% 150% Slightly resistant 25% 75% 85% 100% 125% Resistant 50% 50% 60% 75% 100% Very resistant 75% 25% 35% 50% 75% Immune 100% 0% 10% 25% 50%

Immunity counts as 100% resistance, so penetration lets its own share through an immunity. Against a weakness it adds on top. Physical and spirit damage have no penetration.

items.title: Critical strike damage
items.text:
Critical hits multiply the hit's damage by:

1.5 + critical damage bonuses, at least 0

The bonuses come in parts, each its flat bonuses × (1 + increases): general ones, those for your weapon kind, for the target, and for the alternative attack. The parts are computed separately and added up, so a general "reduced critical damage" doesn't lower your weapon's own bonus.

On a crossbow's last loaded shot (magazine), if you have critical damage increases for that shot, the multiplier is 1 + (0.5 + flat critical damage bonuses) × (1 + every critical damage increase that applies to the shot) × more critical damage: the increases then multiply the base too.

items.title: Critical strike chance
items.text:
Critical strike chance starts from the weapon's base:

chance = (base + flat) × (1 + increases) × more, at most the maximum

Base: knives 15%, polearms 10%, other weapons 5%, spells 5%. The weapon's own critical chance properties apply to its base first. The maximum is 100% by default.

items.title: Evasion
items.text:
Evasion rating gives a chance to avoid a hit, which depends on the attacker's accuracy (enemy accuracy), growing with its level and stars:

accuracy = (30 + 0.48 × level) × (1 + 15% × stars) evade chance = evasion ÷ (3 × accuracy), at most 100%

Each hit is rolled on its own. Every hit you evade lowers your chance against that attacker: × 80% per evasion, until it goes 8 s without hitting you (30 s for a boss). Each evasion costs 18% of your maximum stamina, less with cost reductions for evading; with less stamina than that, you can't evade. Damage over time in an area can't be evaded. Chance against creatures without stars, before any evasion, by biome:

Biome Accuracy 50 evasion 100 evasion 200 evasion 400 evasion Meadows 30 54.68% 100% 100% 100% Black Forest 39 42.6% 85.21% 100% 100% Swamp 51 32.91% 65.82% 100% 100% Mountain 67 24.89% 49.78% 99.56% 100% Plains 77 21.77% 43.54% 87.08% 100% Mistlands 92 18.04% 36.08% 72.15% 100% Ashlands 117 14.26% 28.52% 57.04% 100% Deep North 148 11.26% 22.51% 45.02% 90.04%

items.title: Resistances
items.text:
Resistances reduce damage of their type: damage × (1 − resistance).

resistance = min(cap, your resistance − enemy penetration); cap = 75% + maximum resistance, at most 90%

Fire, frost and lightning also count elemental resistance. Penetration can take resistance below zero, which increases the damage taken.

items.title: Armour
items.text:
Armour is Valheim's own: it reduces each hit by the same share for all its damage types, much against small hits, less against big ones. With hit damage the sum of the hit's damage types:

armour < damage ÷ 2: damage taken = damage − armour; otherwise: damage taken = damage² ÷ (4 × armour) armour against creatures = your armour × 1.05 − the creature's armour penetration

Armour applies after rune shield and block. Creatures ignore part of it: see enemy penetration. Damage taken, by armour and hit:

Armour Hit of 20 Hit of 50 Hit of 100 Hit of 200 Hit of 500 25 4 25 75 175 475 50 2 12.5 50 150 450 100 1 6.2 25 100 400 200 0.5 3.1 12.5 50 300

items.title: Rune shield
items.text:
Rune shield is a layer over your health. Of a hit that gets through block, resistances and armour, it takes everything but spirit and poison damage until it runs out; the rest goes to your health. While it holds, stagger you take is cut by 50%.

maximum = (base + flat + armour's rune shield + food + from health) × (1 + increases)

Valheim's shield effects (such as the Staff of Protection's) become a ward on whoever gets them: it takes Valheim's amount of damage, everything but spirit and poison, for Valheim's duration (on you, longer with buff duration, at most × 3). While a ward holds, stagger taken is cut by 50% too.

The base is 0 by default (a server setting): only the tree, gear and food give a shield. Stats that turn health into shield give maximum health × p ÷ (1 − p) for a share p, at most 90%.

Damage you take restarts the wait. After 5 s without damage, it recharges 20% of its maximum per second (5 s from empty), faster with shield regeneration. Recharge delay reductions cut the wait by at most 75%, never below 0.25 s.

items.title: Enemy penetration
items.text:
Creatures pierce your defences by their biome: with flat armour penetration and resistance penetration (a share of your resistances). Your armour counts for 105% against creatures' hits.

Biome Armour ignored Resistance ignored Meadows 0 0% Black Forest 8 0% Swamp 15 0% Mountain 25 5% Plains 35 10% Mistlands 50 15% Ashlands 70 20% Deep North 90 25%

Bosses move toward the next biome's values. Creatures with the Piercing modifier ignore more.

items.title: Stagger
items.text:
Stagger fills from a hit's blunt, slash, pierce and lightning damage, as the target takes it. At its threshold, maximum health × the creature's own stagger factor, the target staggers. The gauge then drains: from full in 5 s for players, 25 s for enemies (the mod slows it).

Your own threshold counts 100% of your maximum rune shield as health, and your gauge drains that much faster, so it still empties in the same time.

your hit's stagger = (damage × 20% + flat) × (1 + stagger build-up) × the weapon's stagger multiplier

Your hits carry 20% of the stagger power Valheim gives them (a server setting); stagger build-up multiplies it and flat stagger build-up adds to it.

Forced stagger: when it rolls, the hit's stagger is multiplied by 100.

Stagger you take: × (1 − stagger resistance), which is at most 85%; cut by 50% while your rune shield holds. Stagger recovery drains your gauge faster.

items.title: Block
items.text:
Block: when you block a hit from the front, Valheim treats your block power like armour against the whole hit, every damage type, after the blocking item's own resistances.

block power = max(0, Valheim's block power × (1 + the shield's own block power increases) + flat block power) × (1 + block power increases) Valheim's block power = the item's block power at its quality × (1 + Blocking skill × 0.5) parry: block power × the item's parry bonus × (1 + parry bonus increases)

A parry is a block within 0.25 s of raising your guard, with an item that has a parry bonus. A block costs Valheim's block stamina × the share of your block power the hit used; a parry costs a fixed amount.

What gets through works like armour: block power under half the hit takes that much off; more than that cuts the hit to hit² ÷ (4 × block power). The rest goes on to your armour and rune shield.

If you're out of stamina, or the blocked hit's stagger breaks your guard, nothing is blocked. A hit that meets your block can't be a Glancing Blow.

items.title: Glancing blows
items.text:
Glancing Blow: any hit a creature lands on you that doesn't meet your block can glance. Everyone has 25% chance (a server setting), plus glancing blow chance.

glancing blow: damage taken − 35% × (1 + glancing blow reduction increases), that cut kept between 5% and 90%

The cut joins your other damage-taken modifiers, which together can take off at most 60%. It comes before your resistances, block and armour.

Hits that meet your block don't glance; with Edge of the Block, a blocked hit that breaks your guard still can.

items.title: Endurance
items.text:
Endurance: while your health is under your endurance threshold, the part of any damage you take below the threshold is reduced, hits and damage over time alike.

damage taken = damage − (the part of it below the threshold) × endurance reduction

Reduction is 20% at base, × (1 + increases), at most 75%. The threshold is in health points; with Rune Line it's compared to your rune shield instead.

It applies last, after your resistances, block and armour, just before your rune shield takes the damage.

items.title: Thorns
items.text:
Thorns: when a creature hits you and you don't evade it, it takes your thorns damage back. The amount doesn't depend on the hit: it's your flat thorns, or 5 if increased thorns are all you have.

thorns damage = flat thorns × (1 + damage increases + thorns increases + the damage type's increases) × block or parry multiplier × distance

It's pierce damage, unless your stats convert part of it to other types or add more as extra damage.

Full damage to an attacker within 3 m of you (from its edge), falling to nothing at 8 m.

On a shield block with Spiked Shield: × 150%. Thorns that work with parries add to a parry's thorns.

Thorny Carapace also deals your thorns to enemies touching you, once every 1 s per enemy, shorter with cooldown recovery.

items.title: Charged attacks
items.text:
Charged attack: something charges your next weapon attack, and the next melee or ranged attack you release spends it, hit or miss (spells only with ChargeApplicability). One charge waits at a time; it doesn't stack or expire.

charged attack: + 25% increased damage, added to your other damage increases, and rows that work with charged attacks apply

A source charges again only 2 s after it last charged the attack (critical hits: 0.2 s). After any charge, every source also waits the shorter of its own cooldown and 3 s (cut by cooldown recovery). A perfect dodge ignores both cooldowns, but can't charge an attack that's already charged.

What charges the attack. Each source needs the passive or mastery option that grants it:

Charges the attack when Granted by an alternative attack hits an enemy Second edge you activate a trinket Flash Response you cast a spell Spell Primes the Strike you cover 25 m running on the ground or levitating, while no charge waits Giant's Run-Up you jump Leap Before the Blow you land a critical hit with an attack Critical Charge you parry a hit Ready Answer you start a dodge roll (a perfect dodge charges it even on cooldown) Rolling Charge

With Choose the Spend, only alternative attacks spend the charge; with Alternate Leads, alternative attacks don't spend it.

Unbound Charge: rolled once when the charge is spent. On success the attack gets 50% increased damage instead, and every row that works with charged attacks counts twice.

Hit splash: a charged attack's first hit on an enemy also hits every other enemy within 3 m × (1 + area of effect increases), for your splash share of its damage.

items.title: Additional strikes
items.text:
Strike: a melee weapon's vertical swing, primary or alternative (horizontal swings and thrusts don't count, whatever their animation); slams and sceptres don't count. Once a swing hits an enemy, it hits again as many times as your additional strikes, one every 0.12 s. Each goes to the nearest enemy not struck yet, within 5 m of the first target and 4.5 m of you; when there is none left, they stop.

additional strikes = ⌊additional strikes⌋, ×2 once after a critical strike (Double on Crit)

Each additional strike is a new hit of the same attack: it rolls its own critical strike and gets all your damage bonuses. Strike bonuses apply to the swing and to every additional strike.

With Double on Crit, the attack's first critical strike, from the swing or from one of its strikes, doubles its additional strikes, once per attack.

With All on One Target, every additional strike hits the first target instead, at 50% damage each, and they stop if it dies or gets out of reach.

Combo counts one hit per attack: additional strikes and phantom strikes never add to it.

Primary attacks that are strikes: Antler Pickaxe, Black Metal Pickaxe, Bronze Pickaxe, Iron Pickaxe, Stone Pickaxe.

Alternative attacks that are strikes: Black Metal Axe, Bloodgeon, Bronze Axe, Bronze Mace, Flametal Mace, Flint Axe, Frostfire Axe, Frostfire Mace, Frostner, Iron Axe, Iron Mace, Jotun Bane, Klossen, Nord Axe, Nord Mace, Porcupine, Stone Axe, Storm Star, Thunderblood Axe, Thunderblood Mace, Wooden Axe, Wooden Mace.

items.title: Phantom strikes
items.text:
Phantom Strikes can follow a melee attack hit: the weapon's own blow or one of its additional strikes, not projectiles, area blows or other copies. Each hits a random enemy within 6 m of the struck one, that one included: the first 0.15 s after the hit, then one every 0.1 s.

phantom strikes per hit = ⌊chance⌋, +1 with a probability of what is left phantom strike damage = 24% × the hit's damage without its critical strike

The hit's damage is taken with all your damage bonuses applied but its critical hit taken out, before the enemy's armour and resistances. A phantom strike doesn't get your bonuses again, but it rolls a critical strike of its own: your weapon's crit chance against the enemy it hits (with rows for phantom strikes), and your weapon's crit multiplier. The enemy's armour and resistances apply to it as usual.

Stagger: a phantom strike carries 50% of the hit's stagger, with the stagger build-up that works with phantom strikes in place of the hit's own.

Ailment gauge: phantom strikes don't fill it. Their fire, poison and spirit damage hits at once instead of over time, and their frost and lightning bring no chill or shock.

With Endless Apparition, a phantom strike that lands can cause more: the n-th generation's chance is the first's × the factor its line gives, to the power n − 1. At most 96 phantom strikes wait at once.

items.title: Area of effect
items.text:
Area of effect widens attacks in a straight line: the factor multiplies the hit radius, not the ground it covers. +100% area doubles the radius and covers four times the ground.

radius × max(0.1, (1 + area increases) × area multipliers)

Area attacks (a slam is one) get the wider radius; other swings reach further as well.

items.title: Slams and aftershocks
items.text:
Slam: Valheim's area attacks (the sledge's swing and others like it) count, and so does an alternative attack Ground Strike turns into one: it uses the weapon's own area radius, or 3 m if the weapon has no area attack. Your area of effect widens a slam's radius.

Aftershock: rolled once per slam, at most 100%. 0.45 s later it erupts at the slam's point, in the slam's radius × the area increases that only apply to aftershocks, and hits everything there with the slam's full damage. An aftershock never rolls another, though repeat chance can make it erupt once more.

An aftershock pushes enemies away from where it erupts.

A thrown club, mace or sledge that lands on the ground (not on a creature) slams there once: 3 m × your area of effect, with 100% of the weapon's damage × your skill multiplier, against every enemy and object in it. A thrown sceptre that lands casts its spell there instead.

A charged attack that isn't a slam can make aftershocks too, from aftershock chance that works with charged attacks: each full 100% gives one, and the rest is a chance for one more, each 0.45 s after the last, where the enemy was hit.

Primary attacks that are slams: Demolisher, Frostfire Sledge, Iron Sledge, Nord Sledge, Stagbreaker, Thunderblood Sledge, Wooden Sledge.

Alternative attacks that Ground Strike turns into slams: Battleaxe, Berserkir Axes, Black Metal Atgeir, Black Metal Battleaxe, Bleeding Berserkir Axes, Bronze Atgeir, Brutal Slayer, Crystal Battleaxe, Demolisher, Early Axes, Frostfire Atgeir, Frostfire Greataxe, Frostfire Greatsword, Frostfire Sledge, Himminafl, Iron Atgeir, Iron Sledge, Krom, Nord Atgeir, Nord Greataxe, Nord Greatsword, Nord Sledge, Primal Berserkir Axes, Primal Slayer, Scourging Slayer, Skull Splittur, Slayer, Stagbreaker, Thunderblood Atgeir, Thunderblood Greataxe, Thunderblood Greatsword, Thunderblood Sledge, Thundering Berserkir Axes, Wooden Atgeir, Wooden Battleaxe, Wooden Greatsword, Wooden Sledge.

items.title: Ailments
items.text:
Ailment gauge: bleeding, burning, poison, chill and shock each fill their own on the enemy, from the matching part of your hits' damage as the enemy takes it, after its resistances and armour: slash, fire, poison, frost and lightning.

gauge filled by a hit = matching damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up)

How much of the gauge one hit fills, by its damage as a share of the enemy's base health (its maximum health without the mod's difficulty scaling):

Damage ÷ base health 5% 10% 25% 50% Filled, +0% build-up 8% 16% 40% 80% Filled, +100% build-up 16% 32% 80% 100%

At 100% the ailment starts, from the strongest matching hit since the gauge began to fill. The gauge then stays full, so every further matching hit applies the ailment again from its own damage. 3 s after the last matching hit the gauge drains, 25% per second. Chill ends when it is empty (at most 7 s after that hit); the other ailments run their own time.

What each ailment does with that damage:

  • Bleeding: 20% of the slash damage per second for 4 s (80% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (physical). Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One bleed per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second.
  • Burning: 25% of the fire damage per second for 4 s (100% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (fire); fire damage increases don't apply again. Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One burn per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second. A wet enemy burns out 6 times as fast.
  • Poison: 15% of the poison damage per second for 4 s (60% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (poison), plus any share of the enemy's base health your stats add, spread over the same 4 s (ailment damage doesn't raise that part). Longer duration adds seconds. Each player can keep 3 poisons on an enemy (more with limit bonuses); past that, a new one replaces your weakest if it would deal more. Skeletons and the Charred take poison damage normally, but their poison gauge fills at half speed; summoned skeletons stay immune.
  • Chill: Valheim's frost effect, its strength × (1 + your general and chill ailment damage increases); ailment and status duration make it last longer.

  • Shock: for 3 s the enemy takes more damage from every source and builds up stagger faster, by the shock's strength. Only the strongest shock on an enemy acts, whoever applied it. Flat ailment damage does nothing for shock.

    shock strength = 0.5 × (lightning damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health))^0.4 × (1 + shock effect increases) × more, at most 50%; under 5%, no shock

    The lightning damage here is the hit's, before the enemy's resistances and armour.

Ailment damage multipliers for burning, poison and bleeding: × (1 + ailment damage increases, general and that ailment's) × their more multipliers; flat ailment damage adds its amount spread over 4 s. Each player's ailments tick on their own, once a second.

items.title: Armour break
items.text:
Armour break: a hit's blunt damage breaks the enemy's armour the way it would fill an ailment gauge: blunt against its base health, raised by build-up. The broken share adds up to 100% and is shared by everyone hitting the enemy; 8 s after the last hit that added to it, it's gone.

broken share added by a hit = blunt ÷ (ailment threshold × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up) your physical damage + the enemy's armour × broken share × (1 + armour break effect increases), that share at most 100%

Every hit of yours on an enemy with broken armour gets that added, including the hit that just added to it, spread over its blunt, slash and pierce (as blunt if it has none). It comes before the enemy's armour, so it pays back about as much as the armour takes.

items.title: Impale
items.text:
Impale: a hit's pierce damage can impale the enemy. The chance works like the ailment gauge: pierce against the enemy's base health, raised by build-up.

chance = (pierce ÷ (ailment threshold × the enemy's base health) + flat build-up) × (1 + build-up increases), at most 100% physical damage your hits deal × (1 + impales × 5% × (1 + ailment damage increases))

An enemy holds up to 5 impales (more with impale limit). Each new impale refreshes them all for 8 s × (1 + ailment duration increases), at least 0.5 s.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
Limit: a bonus that names an effect raises only that effect. One that names none raises every limit below at once. Bonuses add up first, and the total is rounded down (but not for the infusion store).

Limit Base Thralls per cast of a summoning staff 1 Spores at once 3 Ice crystals at once 3 Armour shards at once 3 Impales one enemy can hold 5 Links you can hold at once 1 Ground Effects: patches at once 1 Infusion: units stored 10

Chain Lightning's targets (3) are the exception: they only count limit bonuses that name Chain Lightning.

items.title: Ground effects
items.text:
Ground Effects: a passive that creates ground for a damage type (Ashen Wake, Blighted Soil, Glassbound, Stormbed) makes your spells leave a patch where they land: a projectile that hits the ground or an object (not one that hits an enemy), or an area spell where it strikes. One impact makes one patch, with a layer for each of the spell's fire, frost, lightning and poison damage that has such a passive.

Each layer comes from the spell's damage of its type, after your damage increases (ground damage increases join them) and before its critical strike:

damage per second = 20% × that damage × your damage over time multiplier for the type build-up per second = 20% × that damage, into burning, chill, shock or poison

A patch has a radius of 2 m × (1 + area increases; a spell's patch also takes spell area increases), at most 12 m, and lasts 4 s × (1 + effect duration increases), at most 60 s.

Enemies standing on it (on the ground, not swimming) take its damage every 0.2 s, paid about once a second, through their resistances. Ground damage is never a critical strike, can't be blocked or evaded, and doesn't stagger. Each enemy takes only the strongest patch of each type, whoever made it; different types add up. Your allies and you take no damage from your patches.

You can keep 1 patch at once (limits); a new one past the limit removes your oldest. Only spell patches count.

Chilled Ground makes everyone on it slide, you and your allies too. It doesn't lower speed: speeding up and braking work at 15% of the usual rate, turning at 35%.

Passives that work while you stand on a kind of ground count any patch of that type, yours or not.

items.title: Infusion
items.text:
Infusion: with Gather the Elements and a staff in hand (elemental or blood magic), standing on your own spell patches absorbs them into a store, by damage type. A patch shrinks as it's absorbed and is gone below 0.3 m.

units gained = 6 m² per second × (1 + absorption rate) ÷ 2 m²

Less is gained where your other patches of the same type already cover the patch's edge.

The store holds at most 10 units in all (limits). It empties 10 s after the last gain, and when you die.

Your next damaging spell cast by hand (or attack with Sceptre of the Pious) uses the whole store: each unit adds 6% of the damage of the spell that made the patch (that type, after its increases) × (1 + infusion potency), as flat damage of its type. A projectile spell splits it among its projectiles; an area spell adds all of it to every hit. Damage that came from infusion can't be absorbed again.

Spell Echo repeats infused projectile spells; infused area spells aren't repeated.

items.title: Life leech
items.text:
Life leech: a share of the health your weapon and projectile hits actually remove from an enemy; spells use spell leech. Bleeding, thorns and echoed hits don't leech.

leeched = health removed × life leech

Each hit starts its own leech, which gives back 2% of your maximum health per second until it's paid out. All of them together give at most 20% per second, which 10 leeches running at once reach. Reaching full health ends every leech still running.

items.title: Build cost
items.text:
Build cost reductions lower each material of a piece, the mod's buildings included, by at most 50%:

cost = ⌈amount × (1 − reduction)⌉, reduction at most 50%

Dismantling gives back only what was paid. When a refund saves the materials of a placed piece, dismantling it gives nothing.

Data from Path of Valheiman 5.3.2, extracted 2026-10-24.

items.title: Creature scaling
items.text:
How the game sets a creature's level, health and damage, and what stars, difficulty, defeated bosses and Monster Power change.

Numbers are the defaults of the Normal difficulty; servers can change them. Every formula here is checked against the mod's code with each patch.

items.title: Health and damage
items.text:
A creature's health and damage are Valheim's own, multiplied by these factors:

Health = base health × biome × (1 + star bonus × stars) × tamed × Monster Power × Blight Mist Damage = base damage × biome × (1 + star bonus × stars) × tamed × Monster Power × Blight Mist

Biome: the factor of the creature's biome (table below; bosses use the boss columns). Stars: see Stars. Tamed: a tamed creature has 50% of it. Monster Power: see Monster Power. Blight Mist: only inside a mist. Valheim's own world difficulty settings apply on top.

items.title: Biome factors
items.text:
A creature's biome is its kind's home biome, wherever it stands: a Greydwarf counts as a Black Forest creature everywhere. Kinds the mod doesn't know take the biome they stand in.

Biome Health Damage Boss health Boss damage Meadows ×1 ×1 ×1.65 ×1.025 Black Forest ×1.2 ×1.05 ×1.8 ×1.05 Swamp ×1.35 ×0.99 ×2.25 ×1.1 Mountain ×2.052 ×1.35 ×2.85 ×1.25 Plains ×2.88 ×1.4 ×3.6 ×1.4 Mistlands ×3 ×1.7 ×4.5 ×1.7 Ashlands ×3.5 ×2 ×5.25 ×2 Deep North ×4 ×2.3 ×6 ×2.3

Some kinds have their own health factor, which replaces the biome's: Wolf ×6, Draugr ×3.6.

Some bosses get one more health factor on top: Bonemass ×1.2, Yagluth ×1.2.

These keep their own health: Kall Fimbulbringer.

Minions: your summons scale on their own, see summon strength.

items.title: Difficulty presets
items.text:
The difficulty preset scales how far every biome factor is from 1, and sets the star chance and the most stars a creature can have:

factor = 1 + (biome factor − 1) × scale Preset Health scale Damage scale Star chance Most stars Vanilla 0 0 10% 2 Easy 0.2 0.25 12% 4 Normal 1 1 18% 5 Hard 1.2 1.5 24% 7 Merciless 1.5 2 30% 8

items.title: After a biome's boss
items.text:
Once a biome's boss has been defeated, the creatures of that biome move part of the way toward the next biome's factors (health, damage and penetration): 25% near the world centre, up to 80% far from it. Bosses don't step up, and nor does the Deep North.

step = 0.25 + (0.8 − 0.25) × t, t = (distance from the world centre − near) ÷ (far − near), from 0 to 1 Biome From (near) Full step (far) Meadows 0 m 5000 m Black Forest 600 m 6000 m Swamp 2000 m 6000 m Mountain 1000 m 9000 m Plains 3000 m 8000 m Mistlands 6000 m 10000 m Ashlands 8000 m 10500 m

Wolves and Draugr keep their own health factor, so only their damage steps up.

items.title: Stars
items.text:
Stars make a creature stronger, set its rarity and bring modifiers.

Health × (1 + 1 × stars) Damage × (1 + 0.5 × stars)

Each star step has a 18% chance (Valheim: 10%), rolled until it fails, up to two stars; hostile creatures in their home biome can always reach 2. A creature with two stars then gains another star with a 50% chance each time, up to the preset's most stars. Each star brings 1 modifier. Chances of the first roll:

Stars Chance 0 82% 1 14.76% 2+ 3.24%

items.title: Boss stars
items.text:
A boss summoned at its altar can rise with stars: a 25% chance of at least one star, and 5% of two (part of the 25%). By default, only once that boss has been defeated in the world. Runes of the Blood Challenge (up to 5) offered at a boss altar, Valheim's or that of one of the mod's bosses, give the next boss summoned there one star each instead of the roll, even before its first defeat, with at least one modifier per star.

Health × (1 + 0.5 × stars) Damage × (1 + 0.25 × stars)

Modifiers per boss star: 0 on Normal, 1 on Hard and Merciless.

items.title: Monster Power
items.text:
Offering boss trophies at an Altar of Power makes the creatures of that biome stronger, and more of them:

Monster Power = 1 + 0.1 × offerings, at most ×5

It multiplies the health and damage of the biome's wild creatures, bosses included (not tamed ones), but doesn't add to their loot. Each offering also raises the biome's hostile population by 5%: as many more of its wild creatures (not bosses) can be around at once, and they spawn as much faster. Monster Power reaches its maximum after 40 offerings; each offering costs one trophy more than the last.

Data from Path of Valheiman 5.3.2, extracted 2026-10-24.

items.title: Experience and levels
items.text:
Area levels, item levels, where experience comes from, how it falls off, and what each character level costs.

Numbers are the defaults of the Normal difficulty; servers can change them. Every formula here is checked against the mod's code with each patch.

items.title: Area levels
items.text:
Every biome has a fixed level. A creature's level is the level of the biome it stands in (stars don't change it): it sets the creature's accuracy and the item level of its loot, a chest takes the level of its biome, and gear bought from a trader the level of the biome the trader is in. It doesn't scale health or damage, except for the monolith bosses. With the Raid level scaling setting (off by default, on in Merciless), raiders take the level of the biome the raid comes from, and scale with it. Each biome also has a recommended player level: up to the next biome's, it gives full experience; past it, experience falls off.

A creature in the Blight Mist takes the level of the next boss's biome by the world's progress (the first boss not yet defeated; the Deep North once Fader is), wherever it stands.

Biome Level Full experience up to level Meadows 1 19 Black Forest 19 43 Swamp 43 77 Mountain 77 97 Plains 97 130 Mistlands 130 181 Ashlands 181 246 Deep North 246 311

items.title: Item level
items.text:
A dropped item takes the level of the creature that drops it, or of the chest's biome (area levels).

A crafted item's level is the highest level among its materials, by the biome they come from; materials a recipe only needs for upgrades don't count. Moulds count as the Deep North, idols as the biome of their tier (below). Each item base shows its own. It is the level used when runes add properties to the item: each rune sets it again from the recipe.

The level each upgrade idol counts as:

Idol Biome Level Wooden Battle Idol / Wooden Protection Idol Meadows 1 Bronze Battle Idol / Bronze Protection Idol Black Forest 19 Iron Battle Idol / Iron Protection Idol Swamp 43 Silver Battle Idol / Silver Protection Idol Mountain 77 Black Metal Battle Idol / Black Metal Protection Idol Plains 97 Black Marble Battle Idol / Black Marble Protection Idol Mistlands 130 Flametal Battle Idol / Flametal Protection Idol Ashlands 181 Bloodgold Battle Idol / Bloodgold Protection Idol Deep North 246

Item level decides which properties and tiers can roll (each tier has a level range), how rare drops are, and which uniques can drop.

An item ascended with a boss essence has at least the level of its new biome.

items.title: Experience
items.text:
Only combat raises your character level: kills, and the hits of your fighting skills. Everything peaceful (gathering, building, crafting, exploring, travelling) goes to craft experience instead, and the experience fall-off never cuts it.

Experience from a kill:

Experience = base health × 0.4 × (1 + 0.5 × stars + 0.5 × modifiers)

Base health is the Valheim health of its kind. It is shared between the players alive within 40 m (2.5× that for bosses). At night, every experience gain is +50%. Creatures of a runic event give 10%.

items.title: Experience fall-off
items.text:
Past a biome's recommended range, the combat experience you gain there fades. The ranges follow the recommended player levels (a server setting, by default the biomes' levels). The level that counts is yours; the biome is where the creature dies (for kills) or where you stand (for hits). Being below a biome's level costs nothing.

kept = max(0.05, 0.05 ^ (levels past the range ÷ 10))

Experience fades to 5% at 10 levels past the range, and never lower:

Levels past the range +1 +2 +3 +5 +8 +10 Experience kept 74.11% 54.93% 40.71% 22.36% 9.1% 5% Biome Full experience 5% from level Meadows 1–19 29 Black Forest 19–43 53 Swamp 43–77 87 Mountain 77–97 107 Plains 97–130 140 Mistlands 130–181 191 Ashlands 181–246 256 Deep North 246–311 321

items.title: Kills by allies
items.text: A kill by your minions, pets or companions gives 100% of a normal kill's experience, shared between the players nearby like any kill's (2.5× the reach for bosses). If you hit the creature yourself in the last 10 s, you get the normal kill instead.

items.title: Character level
items.text:
Combat experience raises your character level, up to 200. Each level needs:

experience to the next level = 20.7 × level ^ 1.1, rounded Level To the next level Total to reach 2 44 21 10 261 1,112 25 714 8,143 50 1,531 35,676 75 2,391 84,192 100 3,281 154,589 125 4,193 247,519 150 5,125 363,494 175 6,072 502,944 200 — 666,239

Each level gives 1 passive point; points also come from other sources.

On death you lose 10% of a level's experience (experience lost on death), never going below the start of your level. Passives can lower the loss.

items.title: Permadeath
items.text:
The server setting Permadeath mode (off by default) makes death permanent in the ways chosen with its other settings, each off by default:

  • Permadeath: destroy all items: everything you carry and wear is destroyed, with no tombstone.
  • Permadeath: reset the combat tree: back to level 1 with no experience, only the start allocated.
  • Permadeath: reset the craft tree: all crafting progress is lost.
  • Permadeath: no Blink and Mirror creatures: creatures never get those two modifiers.
  • Permadeath: one-shot guard: a hit that would kill you and deals more than 95% of your maximum health leaves you at 1 health instead, at most once every 30 minutes of world time.
  • Permadeath: right to a mistake: one death is forgiven and works like an ordinary death; the right comes back after 2 hours of play.

Data from Path of Valheiman 5.3.2, extracted 2026-10-24.

items.title: Loot and experience
items.text:
What a kill gives: Path of Valheiman loot, Valheim's own drops, and experience.

Numbers are the defaults of the Normal difficulty; servers can change them. Every formula here is checked against the mod's code with each patch.

items.title: Loot
items.text:
When a creature dies, its Path of Valheiman loot is rolled with two numbers, item quantity and item rarity:

Quantity = 1 + item quantity + 0.1 × stars + 0.5 × modifiers Rarity = item rarity + 0.2 × stars

Item quantity and item rarity are the killer's own, from passives and gear. Modifiers add quantity, not rarity. A kill by one of your summons, companions or pets counts as yours. The loot's item level is the creature's level; uniques and jewels keep it too (shown with Alt).

A creature, elite or boss killed in the Blight Mist also has a 0.2% chance to drop Womb of Corruption.

On a difficulty preset with more stars than Normal, creatures and elites (not bosses or chests) give less per star: the star and modifier terms of quantity and rarity are × the preset's star share, and their quantity × its quantity factor, so that loot per area stays near Normal's:

Preset Star share Quantity factor Vanilla 100% 100% Easy 100% 100% Normal 100% 100% Hard 68.12% 73.76% Merciless 50.3% 55.48%

items.title: Drops per kill
items.text:
Each kind rolls its own number of drops: on average this many × quantity.

Source Equipment Currency Jewels Creature 1 in 77 1 in 67 1 in 846 Elite creature 1 in 14 1 in 22 1 in 107 Boss 1 in 3 1 in 7 1 in 16 Chest 1 in 4 1 in 17 1 in 31 Dungeon chest 1 in 3 1 in 14 1 in 36

By default, a piece of equipment only drops once you know its recipe (all its materials); currency, jewels and uniques have no such gate. Servers can switch each kind off per source (enemies, bosses, chests) and change their rates.

items.title: Rarity by item level
items.text:
Gear never drops common: it is magic or rare, by these weights, which rarity shifts toward rare. Base jewels can also drop common, with a weight of 25% of the magic one (after rarity):

c = rarity ÷ (1 + rarity); magic × (1 + c), rare × (1 + 2c) Level Common Magic Rare 1 90 9.5 0.5 19 78 19 3 43 62 29 9 77 54 33 13 97 50 34 16 130 45 36 19 181 40 37 23

Each gear drop has a 0.05% × (1 + c) chance to be a unique instead. Bosses always drop at least a magic item, a rare one from level 43.

items.title: Valheim drops
items.text:
Valheim's own drops (meat, hides...) grow with stars; trophies and single items don't.

amount × (1 + 0.5 × stars), at most 100

Except for bosses, the star bonus is × the difficulty preset's star share.

items.title: Ascension
items.text:
A boss essence ascends a weapon, a shield or a summoning staff to a later biome, once per item and only upward: the item's own biome (that of the highest-level material in its recipe; a staff's thrall's) must come before the essence's.

Essence Biome Level Essence of Eikthyr Black Forest 19 Essence of the Elder Swamp 43 Essence of Bonemass Mountain 77 Essence of Moder Plains 97 Essence of Yagluth Mistlands 130 Essence of the Queen Ashlands 181 Essence of Fader Deep North 246 Essence of Kall Deep North 246

The item's base stats are compared with Valheim's own items of its kind from that biome (weapon kind and one- or two-handed, or kind of shield) and raised to their median; they never go down:

  • weapons: combat damage (everything but chopping and mining) rises to the median of that kind's weapons in the biome, keeping its damage types; so does damage per quality level. Kinds with no Valheim weapon in the biome, elemental staves and sceptres rise by how much weapon damage grows from biome to biome.
  • shields: block armour and block force, and their gain per quality level, become at least those of the biome's median shield of that kind.
  • summoning staves: the staff itself doesn't change, but its thralls are called as of the new biome (summon strength).
  • durability and its gain per quality level become at least the biome's.

The item goes back to quality 1, and upgrading it costs what the biome's reference item costs, at that item's station. Its item level rises to the biome's level. Properties, sockets and sigils stay. Corrupted and unidentified items can't ascend, nor pickaxes, bombs, traps, torches or weapons with less than 5 combat damage.

An upgraded item keeps at least the damage, block, parry force and durability it had at its quality.

Valheim's own summoning staves can ascend only while the server setting Vanilla summoning staves is off.

items.title: Dismantling into dust
items.text:
Magic, rare, unique and legendary items can be dismantled into dust at the rune carver's table (this is not salvaging items, which returns recipe materials). Each property of the item is worth the azurite dust price of a rune, by its place among the item's properties; an item with no properties counts as one:

  • property 1: Rune of Spark, 15 azurite dust
  • property 2: Rune of Weaving, 20 azurite dust
  • property 3: Great Rune of the Jarl, 0 azurite dust
  • property 4 and every one after: Great Rune of Ascent, 0 azurite dust
dust = Σ rune price × tier multiplier; uniques and legendaries: dust × 40 × (1 + item level ÷ 100)azurite dust = dust × 0.3, rounded, at least 1uniques: divine dust = ⌊azurite dust × 0.1 ÷ 2⌋, at least 1; legendaries: ⌊azurite dust × 0.2 ÷ 2⌋, at least 1; the azurite dust then loses 2 for each divine dust

A property counts with its tier's multiplier; one without a tier counts ×1. A rune bought with other dust than azurite dust is worth nothing here.

Tier Multiplier T0 ×2 T1 ×1.45 T2 ×1.2 T3 ×1 T4 ×0.85 T5 ×0.7

What an item gives with properties of tier T3 (×1); uniques and legendaries at item level 100 (azurite + divine dust):

Properties Magic or rare Unique Legendary 1 4 324 + 18 288 + 36 2 10 756 + 42 672 + 84 3 10 756 + 42 672 + 84 4 10 756 + 42 672 + 84 5 10 756 + 42 672 + 84 6 10 756 + 42 672 + 84

Unique jewels give dust by their item level instead: see Dismantling unique jewels.

items.title: Dismantling unique jewels
items.text:
Dismantling a unique jewel gives divine dust and azurite dust by its item level:

divine dust = 40 × (1 + (item level − 1) ÷ 249); azurite dust = 10 × (1 + (item level − 1) ÷ 249); both rounded Biome Level Divine dust Azurite dust Meadows 1 40 10 Black Forest 19 43 11 Swamp 43 47 12 Mountain 77 52 13 Plains 97 55 14 Mistlands 130 61 15 Ashlands 181 69 17 Deep North 246 79 20

At the rune carver's table, each dismantle takes at most 0.5 s.

items.title: Summons
items.text:
Summoning staves and their thralls, the eitr they hold, how long they live, how strong they are, and what your stats for minions do.

Numbers are the defaults of the Normal difficulty; servers can change them. Every formula here is checked against the mod's code with each patch.

items.title: Summoning staves
items.text:
Minions: a summoning staff calls a thrall in front of you that follows you and fights for you. A cast costs stamina only; the thrall holds eitr while it lives (below).

Staff Thrall Biome Health Damage Lifetime Eitr held Stamina per cast Workbench level Bone Call Staff Bone Thrall Meadows 40 6 Blunt 15 s 5 10 1 Grave Call Staff Grave Thrall Black Forest 220 22 Blunt 20 s 30 12 2 Barrow Call Staff Barrow Thrall Swamp 140 18 Slash 25 s 15 14 3 Frostbone Call Staff Frostbone Thrall Mountain 650 65 Slash 30 s 100 16 4 Warbone Call Staff Warbone Thrall Plains 280 34 Blunt 35 s 35 18 5

Each cast calls one thrall. There's no limit on how many stand at once: only your free eitr limits them.

Alternative cast, Sacrifice: kills one of your summons, the one under your crosshair (up to 60 m away) or else the one with the least health. It costs nothing; with no summon around, nothing happens.

Each staff quality above 1 gives its thralls +25% health and makes them hold +15% more eitr.

items.title: Held eitr
items.text:
Eitr a summon holds comes off your maximum eitr while it lives, and eitr above the new maximum is lost.

eitr held = base × (1 + 15% × (staff quality − 1)) ÷ (1 + reservation efficiency for minions)

The divisor is at least 0.1: +100% reservation efficiency halves what a summon holds, −20% makes it hold 25% more. The hold ends when the summon dies or its lifetime ends, and comes back if you log in with your summons still alive.

A summoning staff can't call a thrall unless you have that much eitr free. Valheim's own staves can't be cast at all then.

items.title: Lifetime and withering
items.text:
Summons live for a while and wither as they go: their health can't stay above the share of their lifetime they have left.

lifetime = base lifetime × your effect duration for minions health at most = maximum health × (1 − time alive ÷ lifetime), at least 1

When the lifetime ends, the summon leaves. Its time runs on the world's clock, so it keeps passing while you're away.

Deathless Host: your summons have no lifetime: they don't wither and live until they're killed. If you lose it, the ones still alive get a fresh lifetime from that moment.

items.title: Summon strength
items.text:
Summons don't take a creature's usual scaling: no stars, tamed share, Monster Power or Blight Mist.

summon health or damage = base × the biome's health factor × summon power

The biome is the staff's (in the tables here), with its factor from the biome table, softened by the difficulty preset; health and damage both use the health column. The global enemy offense and defense settings apply too. Health is also × (1 + your minion health increases) and +25% per staff quality above 1. Summon power is only for Valheim's staves (below).

A staff ascended with a boss essence calls its thralls as of the essence's biome when that's later than its own; Valheim's staves too.

items.title: Valheim's summoning staves
items.text:
The server setting Vanilla summoning staves (off by default) decides how Dead Raiser, Staff of the Wild, Trollstav and Spirit Caller work.

Off: a cast costs no eitr or health, there's no summon limit, and staff quality no longer changes the summons. Each summon holds eitr, lives and withers like a thrall, and is scaled as a summon of the staff's biome:

Staff Biome Lifetime Eitr held Health × Damage × Dead Raiser Mistlands 40 s 50 ×1 ×1 Staff of the Wild Ashlands 45 s 45 ×1 ×1 Trollstav Ashlands 50 s 300 ×1 ×3 Spirit Caller Deep North 60 s 450 ×1 ×2

On: they work as in Valheim, with eitr and health per cast, a summon limit by staff quality, and summons that stay.

items.title: Your stats for minions
items.text:
Your stats for minions reach your summons, and some of them your pets:

  • damage: × (1 + minion damage increases) (pets add tamed damage increases)
  • health: × (1 + minion health increases)
  • damage they take: × (1 + minion damage taken), between 40% and 500%
  • ailments on them (burning, poison, frost, shock) last × (1 − minion ailment resistance), at most 90% shorter

Summons the mod manages also get:

  • their fire, frost, lightning, poison and spirit damage taken cut by minion resistance, at most 75%
  • minion armour against hits
  • attack speed × (1 + minion attack speed), at least 30%; movement speed × (1 + minion movement speed), at least 20%
  • a shield of minion shield size, which takes damage first and recharges 20% of itself per second after 3 s without a hit
  • critical strikes: minion crit chance as a chance, for × (1.5 + minion crit damage)
  • they look for enemies within 10 m × (1 + minion aggression)

Shared Rune: for 3 s after you block, your rune shield takes 30% of the damage to your minions.

Last Service: damage that would take a minion below 1 health comes off your rune shield instead.

Both protect pets too, and only while your rune shield lasts.

Unstable Minions: the first time a summon drops below 35% health from a hit, it explodes for 33% of its maximum health as fire damage to enemies within 3 m, and dies.

items.title: How modifiers are picked
items.text:
• Every modifier is equally likely, and a creature never wears the same one twice.
  • A creature wears at most one element: Burning, Chilling, Shocking, Venomous.
  • Blink never rolls on creatures indoors (dungeons and other interiors).
  • Summoned bosses never roll these by default: Bound, Mirror, Splitting, Unbreakable.

items.title: Any beast
items.text:
With the Any Beast mastery you can tame creatures that normally can't be tamed. Animals eat the Boar's foods and take its taming times. items.text:
Masteries in the crafting tree for tamed animals:

Mastery Effect Any Beast Allows normally untamable creatures to be tamed. They still need food and the conditions required for taming. Stable Keeper Interacting with a tamed creature gives it longer feeding duration while near player-built structures. The effect remains on that creature. Beast Bearer You can carry one small tamed animal (up to wolf size: boar, wolf, chicken, young animals) in your arms, through portals too: press [Ctrl] + [E] on it to pick it up and again to set it down. You cannot attack while carrying. An animal you can also ride with Any Saddle is picked up by holding [E] instead: a plain press rides it. Named Herd Shows named tamed creatures on the map.

items.text: Boss · made from Valheim's Stone Golem

items.title: Summoning
items.text:

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Infusion: with Gather the Elements and a staff in hand (elemental or blood magic), standing on your own spell patches absorbs them into a store, by damage type. A patch shrinks as it's absorbed and is gone below 0.3 m.

units gained = 6 m² per second × (1 + absorption rate) ÷ 2 m²

Less is gained where your other patches of the same type already cover the patch's edge.

The store holds at most 10 units in all (limits). It empties 10 s after the last gain, and when you die.

Your next damaging spell cast by hand (or attack with Sceptre of the Pious) uses the whole store: each unit adds 6% of the damage of the spell that made the patch (that type, after its increases) × (1 + infusion potency), as flat damage of its type. A projectile spell splits it among its projectiles; an area spell adds all of it to every hit. Damage that came from infusion can't be absorbed again.

Spell Echo repeats infused projectile spells; infused area spells aren't repeated.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

Your minions explode when their health falls below 35% of maximum, dealing 33% of their maximum health as fire damage to nearby enemies. The minion is consumed. Applies only to your summoned minions. Minion health and applicable minion damage modifiers scale it; your own spell/fire modifiers do not transfer automatically.

items.title: Endless Apparition
items.text:
Keystone · Dexterity · Phantom Strikes · Show on tree

Phantom strikes can trigger phantom strikes×0.75 trigger chance per successive proc with phantom strikes×0.75 Phantom strike chance

items.title: Keyword: Endless Apparition
items.text: Phantom strikes may trigger phantom strikes. Each successive generation multiplies its trigger chance by the listed factor; the separate global phantom-chance penalty also applies. Nearby keeps its existing attack-origin rule.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Phantom Strikes can follow a melee attack hit: the weapon's own blow or one of its additional strikes, not projectiles, area blows or other copies. Each hits a random enemy within 6 m of the struck one, that one included: the first 0.15 s after the hit, then one every 0.1 s.

phantom strikes per hit = ⌊chance⌋, +1 with a probability of what is left phantom strike damage = 24% × the hit's damage without its critical strike

The hit's damage is taken with all your damage bonuses applied but its critical hit taken out, before the enemy's armour and resistances. A phantom strike doesn't get your bonuses again, but it rolls a critical strike of its own: your weapon's crit chance against the enemy it hits (with rows for phantom strikes), and your weapon's crit multiplier. The enemy's armour and resistances apply to it as usual.

Stagger: a phantom strike carries 50% of the hit's stagger, with the stagger build-up that works with phantom strikes in place of the hit's own.

Ailment gauge: phantom strikes don't fill it. Their fire, poison and spirit damage hits at once instead of over time, and their frost and lightning bring no chill or shock.

With Endless Apparition, a phantom strike that lands can cause more: the n-th generation's chance is the first's × the factor its line gives, to the power n − 1. At most 96 phantom strikes wait at once.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Unbound Charge
items.text:
Keystone · Strength and Dexterity · Charged Attacks · Show on tree

+25% chance to double all charged-attack effects×0.5 damage

items.title: Keyword: Unbound Charge
items.text: Roll once for the original charged attack. On success, double its charge-granted numerical bonuses and additional-effect counts, including echo, aftershock and phantom-strike payloads. This is not a second use of the attack. Input permissions, target rules, costs and delays do not double.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Charged attack: something charges your next weapon attack, and the next melee or ranged attack you release spends it, hit or miss (spells only with ChargeApplicability). One charge waits at a time; it doesn't stack or expire.

charged attack: + 25% increased damage, added to your other damage increases, and rows that work with charged attacks apply

A source charges again only 2 s after it last charged the attack (critical hits: 0.2 s). After any charge, every source also waits the shorter of its own cooldown and 3 s (cut by cooldown recovery). A perfect dodge ignores both cooldowns, but can't charge an attack that's already charged.

What charges the attack. Each source needs the passive or mastery option that grants it:

Charges the attack when Granted by an alternative attack hits an enemy Second edge you activate a trinket Flash Response you cast a spell Spell Primes the Strike you cover 25 m running on the ground or levitating, while no charge waits Giant's Run-Up you jump Leap Before the Blow you land a critical hit with an attack Critical Charge you parry a hit Ready Answer you start a dodge roll (a perfect dodge charges it even on cooldown) Rolling Charge

With Choose the Spend, only alternative attacks spend the charge; with Alternate Leads, alternative attacks don't spend it.

Unbound Charge: rolled once when the charge is spent. On success the attack gets 50% increased damage instead, and every row that works with charged attacks counts twice.

Hit splash: a charged attack's first hit on an enemy also hits every other enemy within 3 m × (1 + area of effect increases), for your splash share of its damage.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.
